plain_english_summary: Lets the Corporation build its own educational institutions to train medical and para-medical staff for the ESI system.

title: Benefit not assignable or attachable
text: (1) The right to receive any benefit payment under the Act is not transferable or assignable. (2) No cash benefit under the Act is liable to attachment or sale in execution of any court decree or order.
plain_english_summary: Protects ESI benefits from being sold, transferred, or seized to satisfy the beneficiary's debts.

title: Bar of benefits under other enactments
text: A person entitled to any Act benefit cannot also receive any similar benefit admissible under any other enactment.
plain_english_summary: Prevents claiming duplicate similar benefits under other laws once entitled under this Act.

title: Persons not to commute cash benefits
text: Save as regulations may provide, no person is entitled to commute for a lump sum any disablement benefit admissible under the Act.
plain_english_summary: Generally prevents converting periodical disablement benefit into a one-time lump sum, except as regulations specifically allow.

title: Persons not entitled to receive benefit in certain cases
text: Save as regulations may provide, no person is entitled to sickness benefit or temporary disablement benefit for any day on which he works, is on leave/holiday for which he receives wages, or is on strike.
plain_english_summary: Blocks sickness/temporary-disablement benefit for days when the person is actually working, receiving paid leave/holiday wages, or on strike, avoiding double compensation.

title: Recipients of sickness or disablement benefit to observe conditions
text: A person receiving sickness benefit or (non-permanent) disablement benefit must (a) remain under prescribed medical treatment and follow the treating officer's instructions; (b) not do anything while under treatment that might retard recovery; (c) not leave the treatment area without permission; and (d) submit to examination by an authorised medical officer or other authorised person.
plain_english_summary: Imposes behavioural conditions on benefit recipients-cooperating with treatment, not undermining recovery, staying within the treatment area, and submitting to check-ups-to maintain entitlement.

title: Benefits not to be combined
text: (1) An insured person cannot receive, for the same period, both sickness and maternity benefit, both sickness and temporary disablement benefit, or both maternity and temporary disablement benefit.

sub_structure.2: Where entitled to more than one such benefit, the person may choose which to receive.

plain_english_summary: Prevents stacking of overlapping cash benefits for the same period, letting the claimant choose the applicable one.

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1966, with effect from 17-6-1967. (Formerly on the Corporation's right to recover damages from employer in certain cases.)
plain_english_summary: This section, which previously allowed the Corporation to recover damages from an employer in certain circumstances, has been omitted.

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1966, with effect from 17-6-1967. (Formerly on the Corporation's right to be indemnified in certain cases.)
plain_english_summary: This section, which previously gave the Corporation an indemnity right in certain cases, has been omitted.

title: Corporation's rights where a principal employer fails or neglects to pay any contribution
text: (1) If a principal employer fails/neglects to pay a due contribution, causing an employee to lose or receive a lower benefit, the Corporation may pay the person the full benefit they would otherwise have received, and recover from the employer either (i) the difference between what was actually paid and what the actual contributions justified, or (ii) twice the unpaid contribution, whichever is greater.

sub_structure.2: The recoverable amount may be recovered as an arrear of land revenue or under sections 45C-45-I.

plain_english_summary: Protects employees from losing benefits due to their employer's contribution default, while penalising the defaulting employer by recovering the shortfall (or double the unpaid amount, whichever is more).

title: Liability of owner or occupier of factories, etc., for excessive sickness benefit
text: (1) Where the Corporation considers sickness incidence excessive due to insanitary factory/establishment conditions (or employer neglect of health regulations) or insanitary tenements/lodgings occupied by insured persons (due to owner neglect), it may claim the extra sickness-benefit expenditure from the owner/occupier, referring unresolved claims to the appropriate Government.

sub_structure.2: If the Government finds a prima facie case, it appoints a person or persons to hold an inquiry.
sub_structure.3: If the inquiry proves the excess sickness is due to the owner's/occupier's default or neglect, the inquiry officer(s) determine the extra expenditure amount and who must pay it to the Corporation.
sub_structure.4: Such a determination is enforceable as a civil court money decree.
sub_structure.5: 'Owner' of tenements/lodgings includes the owner's agent and any person entitled to collect rent as the owner's lessee.

plain_english_summary: Lets the Corporation recover extra sickness-benefit costs traceable to an employer's or landlord's neglect of health regulations, through a formal inquiry process culminating in a civilly enforceable determination.

title: Repayment of benefit improperly received
text: (1) A person who receives any benefit or payment without lawful entitlement must repay its value/amount to the Corporation; on death, the representative must repay from the deceased's assets, if any.

sub_structure.2: The value of non-cash benefits received is determined by a regulation-specified authority, whose decision is final.
sub_structure.3: The recoverable amount may be recovered as an arrear of land revenue or under sections 45C-45-I.

plain_english_summary: Requires repayment of wrongly received benefits, with enforcement as land-revenue arrears, including from a deceased recipient's estate.

title: Benefit payable up to and including day of death
text: Except as provided in the section 50 proviso, if a person dies during a period for which they are entitled to a cash benefit, the amount up to and including the day of death is paid to the person nominated in writing (as regulations specify), or, absent nomination, to the heir or legal representative.
plain_english_summary: Ensures cash benefit accrued up to the date of death is paid to a nominee or legal heir rather than being forfeited.

title: Employer not to reduce wages, etc.
text: No employer may, merely because of liability for Act contributions, directly or indirectly reduce an employee's wages, or (except as regulations provide) discontinue or reduce service-condition benefits similar to those conferred by this Act.
plain_english_summary: Prevents employers from offsetting their ESI contribution liability by cutting wages or withdrawing comparable existing benefits.

title: Employer not to dismiss or punish employee during period of sickness, etc.
text: (1) No employer may dismiss, discharge, reduce, or otherwise punish an employee while receiving sickness or maternity benefit; nor (except as regulations provide) while receiving temporary disablement benefit, under medical treatment for sickness, or absent due to certified pregnancy/confinement-related illness rendering them unfit for work.

sub_structure.2: Any dismissal/discharge/reduction notice given during the protected period is invalid and inoperative.

plain_english_summary: Protects employees from adverse employment action while they are on ESI-covered sickness, maternity, or disablement-related leave, voiding any notice of dismissal given during that protected window.

title: Definitions
text: In this Chapter: (a) 'other beneficiaries' means persons other than those insured under the Act; (b) 'Scheme' means a Central Government scheme under section 73B for medical facility to other beneficiaries; (c) 'underutilised hospital' means a hospital not fully utilised by insured persons; (d) 'user charges' means the amount chargeable to other beneficiaries for medical facilities, as notified by the Corporation in consultation with the Central Government.
plain_english_summary: Defines the key terms used to extend ESI hospital facilities, on a paid basis, to people outside the insured-person scheme.

title: Power to frame Scheme
text: Notwithstanding anything else in the Act, the Central Government may, by notification, frame a Scheme for other beneficiaries and their families to receive medical facilities at any underutilised Corporation-established hospital, on payment of user charges.
plain_english_summary: Empowers the Central Government to open up spare capacity at ESI hospitals to non-insured persons for a fee.

title: Collection of user charges
text: User charges collected from other beneficiaries are deemed to be contributions and form part of the Employees' State Insurance Fund.
plain_english_summary: Folds the user-charge revenue from non-insured patients into the main ESI Fund, treating it like a contribution.

title: Scheme for other beneficiaries
text: The Scheme may provide for which other beneficiaries are covered, the time and manner of availing medical facilities, the form for furnishing personal/family particulars, and any other matter necessary for implementing the Scheme.
plain_english_summary: Sets out the range of operational matters the Central Government's Scheme for other beneficiaries may address.

title: Power to amend Scheme
text: The Central Government may, by notification, add to, amend, vary or rescind the Scheme.
plain_english_summary: Gives the Central Government ongoing flexibility to modify or cancel the other-beneficiaries Scheme.

title: Laying of Scheme framed under this Chapter
text: Every Scheme framed under this Chapter must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days (in one or more sessions); if both Houses agree to modify or annul it before the following session ends, the Scheme has effect only as modified, or ceases to have effect, without prejudice to anything previously done under it.
plain_english_summary: Subjects the other-beneficiaries Scheme to the same parliamentary laying and modification/annulment procedure used for delegated legislation elsewhere in the Act.

title: Constitution of Employees' Insurance Court
text: (1) The State Government, by notification, constitutes an Employees' Insurance Court for a specified local area.

sub_structure.2: The Court consists of as many Judges as the State Government thinks fit.
sub_structure.3: A person who is or has been a judicial officer, or a legal practitioner of five years' standing, is qualified to be a Judge.
sub_structure.4: The State Government may appoint the same Court for multiple local areas, or multiple Courts for the same area.
sub_structure.5: Where multiple Courts serve the same area, the State Government may regulate business distribution between them by order.

plain_english_summary: Establishes specialised Employees' Insurance Courts, staffed by judicial officers or experienced legal practitioners, to adjudicate ESI disputes at the local level.

title: Matters to be decided by Employees' Insurance Court
text: (1) Disputes on whether a person is an 'employee' or liable for the employee's contribution, wage/average-daily-wage rate, contribution rate, identity of the principal employer, a person's right to benefit (amount/duration), a section 55A dependants'-benefit review direction, or other disputes between principal employer and Corporation, principal and immediate employer, or a person/employee and the Corporation/employer over contributions, benefits or dues, are decided by the Employees' Insurance Court.

sub_structure.2: The Court also decides claims for recovery of contributions from the principal employer, claims by a principal employer against an immediate employer, claims against a principal employer under section 68, claims under section 70 for improperly received benefits, and any claim for recovery of an admissible benefit.
sub_structure.2A: If a 'disablement question' arises in Court proceedings without a medical board/tribunal decision, the Court directs the Corporation to obtain that decision and then proceeds in accordance with it, except where a section 54A(2) appeal is already before the Court, in which case the Court may itself decide all issues.
sub_structure.2B: A principal employer cannot raise a contribution/dues dispute with the Corporation before the Court unless he has deposited 50% of the amount claimed, though the Court may waive or reduce this for recorded reasons.
sub_structure.3: No Civil Court has jurisdiction over matters that the Act assigns to a medical board, medical appeal tribunal, or the Employees' Insurance Court.

plain_english_summary: Defines the Employees' Insurance Court's broad jurisdiction over the full range of ESI disputes-status, wages, contribution rates, benefit entitlement, and recovery claims-excluding ordinary civil courts, and imposing a 50% pre-deposit condition on employer-side contribution disputes.

title: Institution of proceedings, etc.
text: (1) Subject to the Act and State Government rules, proceedings before the Employees' Insurance Court are instituted in the Court for the local area where the insured person was working when the dispute arose.

sub_structure.2: If the Court finds a matter can be more conveniently handled by another Employees' Insurance Court in the same State, it may transfer it, forwarding the relevant records.
sub_structure.3: The State Government may transfer a pending matter to a Court in another State, with that State's consent.
sub_structure.4: A Court receiving a transferred matter continues proceedings as if originally instituted there.

plain_english_summary: Fixes venue rules for ESI Court proceedings and allows for both intra-State and inter-State transfer of cases for convenience.

title: Commencement of proceedings
text: (1) Proceedings before an Employees' Insurance Court commence by application.

sub_structure.1A: Every application must be made within three years from when the cause of action arose. For a benefit claim, the cause of action arises only when the claim is made in accordance with regulations, within twelve months of it becoming due (or a further period the Court allows on reasonable grounds); for the Corporation's contribution-recovery claim against a principal employer, the cause of action arises when the Corporation first makes the claim, but no claim can be made more than five years after the relevant period; for a principal employer's claim against an immediate employer, the cause of action arises only when evidence of contribution payment is due to be received by the Corporation under regulations.
sub_structure.2: Every application must be in the prescribed form, contain prescribed particulars, and be accompanied by any prescribed fee, per State Government rules made in consultation with the Corporation.

plain_english_summary: Sets a three-year limitation period for ESI Court applications, with specific rules on when the 'cause of action' is deemed to arise for benefit claims, Corporation recovery claims (capped at five years back), and employer-to-employer claims.

title: Powers of Employees' Insurance Court
text: (1) The Court has all the powers of a Civil Court for summoning and enforcing witness attendance, compelling document/object discovery and production, administering oaths and recording evidence, and is deemed a Civil Court under section 195 and Chapter XXVI of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

sub_structure.2: The Court follows State Government-prescribed procedure.
sub_structure.3: Costs incidental to proceedings are, subject to State Government rules, in the Court's discretion.
sub_structure.4: A Court order is enforceable as if it were a civil court decree.

plain_english_summary: Equips the Employees' Insurance Court with full civil-court-style evidentiary powers and decree-enforceability for its orders.

title: Appearance by legal practitioners, etc.
text: Any application, appearance or act required before an Employees' Insurance Court (other than personal appearance as a witness) may be made by a legal practitioner, an authorised registered trade union officer, or, with Court permission, any other authorised person.
plain_english_summary: Allows parties to be represented by lawyers or authorised union officials (or others with the Court's leave) rather than always appearing personally.

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1966, with effect from 28-1-1968. (Formerly on benefit not being admissible unless claimed in time.)
plain_english_summary: This section, formerly imposing a specific time-bar on claiming benefits, has been omitted.

title: Reference to High Court
text: An Employees' Insurance Court may submit any question of law to the High Court for decision, and must then decide the pending question in accordance with that decision.
plain_english_summary: Allows the ESI Court to seek binding guidance from the High Court on questions of law arising in a case.

title: Appeal
text: (1) Save as expressly provided, no appeal lies from an Employees' Insurance Court order.

sub_structure.2: An appeal lies to the High Court from a Court order if it involves a substantial question of law.
sub_structure.3: The limitation period for such an appeal is sixty days.
sub_structure.4: Sections 5 and 12 of the Limitation Act, 1963 apply to appeals under this section.

plain_english_summary: Restricts appeals from Employees' Insurance Court orders to the High Court, and only on substantial questions of law, within a sixty-day limitation period (with standard Limitation Act extensions available).

title: Stay of payment pending appeal
text: Where the Corporation has appealed against an Employees' Insurance Court order, that Court may (and must, if directed by the High Court) withhold payment of any sum ordered, pending the appeal's decision.
plain_english_summary: Allows payment under a contested Court order to be paused while the Corporation's appeal is pending, especially if the High Court so directs.

title: Punishment for false statement
text: Whoever, to increase a payment/benefit, cause an unauthorised payment/benefit, or avoid (or help another avoid) a payment due under the Act, knowingly makes or causes a false statement or representation, is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to two thousand rupees, or both.

sub_structure.proviso: An insured person convicted under this section is not entitled to any cash benefit under the Act for a Central Government-prescribed period.

plain_english_summary: Criminalises fraudulent claims or misrepresentations aimed at gaining or avoiding ESI payments, with a further consequence of losing cash-benefit eligibility for a prescribed period on conviction.

title: Punishment for failure to pay contributions, etc.
text: If any person (a) fails to pay a due contribution, (b) deducts or attempts to deduct the employer's contribution from an employee's wages, (c) reduces wages/privileges/benefits in contravention of section 72, (d) dismisses/discharges/reduces/punishes an employee in contravention of section 73 or a regulation, (e) fails/refuses to submit a required return or files a false return, (f) obstructs an Inspector or Corporation official, or (g) contravenes or fails to comply with any Act/rule/regulation requirement for which no special penalty is provided:

sub_structure.i_a: For failure to pay an employee's contribution that was deducted from wages (clause (a)): imprisonment not less than one year, extendable to three years, and fine of ten thousand rupees.
sub_structure.i_b: For any other failure to pay a contribution (clause (a)): imprisonment not less than six months, extendable to three years, and fine of five thousand rupees; the court may impose a lesser term for adequate and special recorded reasons.
sub_structure.ii: For offences under clauses (b) to (g): imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to four thousand rupees, or both.

plain_english_summary: Sets tiered criminal penalties for contribution non-payment and other violations (illegal wage deduction, retaliatory dismissal, false returns, obstruction), with the harshest mandatory minimums reserved for employers who deduct but don't remit employees' contributions.

title: Enhanced punishment in certain cases after previous conviction
text: A person previously convicted of an offence under the Act who commits the same offence again is punishable, for each subsequent offence, with imprisonment up to two years and a fine of five thousand rupees.

sub_structure.proviso: For repeat failure to pay a due contribution, the punishment is imprisonment up to five years but not less than two years, plus a fine of twenty-five thousand rupees.

plain_english_summary: Imposes escalated, partly mandatory-minimum penalties on repeat offenders, with the harshest treatment for repeated failure to pay contributions.

title: Power to recover damages
text: (1) Where an employer fails to pay a due contribution or other amount, the Corporation may recover, by way of penalty, damages up to the arrears amount as specified in regulations, after giving the employer a reasonable hearing.

sub_structure.1_proviso: The Corporation may reduce or waive such damages for a sick industrial company under a BIFR-sanctioned rehabilitation scheme, subject to regulation-specified terms.
sub_structure.2: Damages recoverable under this section may be recovered as an arrear of land revenue or under sections 45C-45-I.

plain_english_summary: Empowers the Corporation to levy additional financial 'damages' (beyond interest) on defaulting employers, with relief available for genuinely sick industrial companies under formal rehabilitation.

title: Power of Court to make orders
text: (1) Where an employer is convicted for failing to pay a contribution, the Court may, besides any punishment, order him in writing to pay the outstanding contribution and furnish the related return, within a specified (extendable) period.

sub_structure.2: The employer is not further liable during the period allowed by the Court, but if the order is not fully complied with by the deadline, he is deemed to have committed a further offence under section 85 and liable to a fine up to one thousand rupees per day of continued non-compliance thereafter.

plain_english_summary: Gives the convicting court power to directly order payment of the unpaid contribution (and return filing) on top of the criminal penalty, with an escalating daily fine for continued non-compliance.

title: Prosecutions
text: (1) No prosecution may be instituted except by or with the sanction of the Insurance Commissioner or an authorised Corporation officer.

sub_structure.2: No court inferior to a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial Magistrate of the First Class may try an offence under the Act.
sub_structure.3: No court may take cognizance of an offence except on a written complaint.

plain_english_summary: Restricts who can initiate ESI prosecutions and which courts can try them, ensuring a minimum level of official sanction and judicial seniority.

title: Offences by companies
text: (1) Where a company commits an offence, every person in charge of and responsible to the company for its business conduct at the time, as well as the company, is deemed guilty and liable, unless he proves the offence occurred without his knowledge or that he exercised due diligence to prevent it.

sub_structure.2: Where the offence is proved to have been committed with the consent, connivance, or attributable neglect of a director, manager, secretary or other officer, that person is also deemed guilty and liable.
sub_structure.explanation_i: 'Company' means any body corporate and includes a firm and other association of individuals.
sub_structure.explanation_ii: 'Director' means, for a company (other than a firm), a managing director or whole-time director; for a firm, a partner.

plain_english_summary: Extends criminal liability for a company's ESI offence to those in charge of its business and to culpable directors/officers, subject to a due-diligence defence.

title: Exemption of a factory or establishment or class of factories or establishments
text: The appropriate Government may, by notification and subject to specified conditions, exempt any factory/establishment or class thereof in a specified area from the Act's operation for up to one year at a time, renewable.

sub_structure.proviso1: Such exemption may be granted only if employees already receive benefits substantially similar or superior to those under the Act.
sub_structure.proviso2: A renewal application must be made three months before expiry, and decided within two months of receipt.

plain_english_summary: Allows time-limited (renewable, one year at a time) exemption of establishments that already provide comparable or better benefits than the Act, with defined renewal-application timelines.

title: Exemption of persons or class of persons
text: The appropriate Government may, by notification and subject to conditions it deems fit, exempt any person or class of persons employed in a covered factory/establishment (or class thereof) from the Act's operation.
plain_english_summary: Allows exemption of specific categories of employees, rather than entire establishments, from the Act.

title: Corporation to make representation
text: No exemption may be granted or renewed under section 87 or 88 unless the Corporation has been given a reasonable opportunity to make representations, which the appropriate Government must consider.
plain_english_summary: Ensures the Corporation has a voice before any exemption (or renewal) is granted, since exemptions reduce its coverage base.

title: Exemption of factories or establishments belonging to Government or any local authority
text: The appropriate Government may, after consulting the Corporation, by notification and subject to specified conditions, exempt a factory/establishment belonging to a local authority from the Act, if its employees already receive substantially similar or superior benefits.
plain_english_summary: Provides a parallel exemption route for local-authority-owned establishments, conditioned on comparable existing benefits and Corporation consultation.

title: Exemption from one or more provisions of the Act
text: The appropriate Government may, with the Corporation's consent, by notification, exempt employees or a class of employees in a factory/establishment (or class thereof) from one or more provisions relating to benefits under the Act.
plain_english_summary: Allows partial exemption-from specific benefit provisions only-rather than blanket exemption from the whole Act, with the Corporation's consent required.

title: Exemptions to be either prospective or retrospective
text: Any exemption notification under section 87, 88, 90 or 91 may be issued to take effect prospectively from a date specified in it.
plain_english_summary: Clarifies that exemption notifications operate from a specified prospective date (following the 2010 amendment removing the earlier retrospective option).

title: Central Government to be appropriate Government
text: Notwithstanding anything else in the Act, for establishments in States where medical benefit is provided by the Corporation (rather than the State Government), the Central Government is the appropriate Government.
plain_english_summary: Shifts the 'appropriate Government' role to the Centre for establishments in States where the Corporation itself directly provides medical benefit.

title: Misuse of benefits
text: If satisfied that benefits are being misused by insured persons in a factory/establishment, the Central Government may, by published order, disentitle such persons from benefits it thinks fit.

sub_structure.proviso: No such order may be passed without giving a reasonable hearing to the concerned factory/establishment, the insured persons, and registered trade unions with members there.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Central Government power to withdraw benefits from insured persons found to be misusing them, subject to a mandatory hearing for all affected parties.

title: Writing off of losses
text: Subject to Central Government-prescribed conditions, where the Corporation considers contribution, interest and damages due to it irrecoverable, it may sanction writing off that amount finally.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Corporation to formally write off genuinely irrecoverable dues, under conditions prescribed by the Central Government.

title: Power of Central Government to give directions
text: (1) The Central Government may direct a State Government on carrying the Act into execution in that State.

sub_structure.2: The Central Government may also give directions to the Corporation for the Act's efficient administration, which the Corporation must comply with.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Central Government a general supervisory directive power over both State Governments and the Corporation regarding Act implementation.

title: Corporation officers and servants to be public servants
text: All officers and servants of the Corporation are deemed public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.
plain_english_summary: Confers public-servant status (and its associated legal protections/liabilities) on all Corporation staff.

title: Liability in case of transfer of establishment
text: Where an employer transfers a factory/establishment (wholly or partly) by sale, gift, lease, licence or otherwise, the transferor and transferee are jointly and severally liable for contribution/other amounts due for periods up to the transfer date.

sub_structure.proviso: The transferee's liability is limited to the value of assets obtained through the transfer.

plain_english_summary: Prevents ESI liability from being evaded through a business transfer, making both old and new owners jointly liable (with the new owner's exposure capped at the assets received).

title: Contributions, etc., due to Corporation to have priority over other debts
text: Amounts due for ESI contributions or other Act payments, accrued before an insolvency-adjudication or company winding-up order, are deemed included among debts entitled to priority over other debts under the Presidency-towns Insolvency Act, 1909, the Provincial Insolvency Act, 1920, corresponding local insolvency laws, or section 530 of the Companies Act, 1956.
plain_english_summary: Gives ESI dues priority ranking in insolvency and company winding-up distributions, similar to other statutory priority debts like taxes.

title: Delegation of powers
text: The Corporation, and (subject to Corporation regulations) the Standing Committee, may direct that any of their powers/functions be also exercisable by a subordinate officer or authority, in relation to specified matters and conditions.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Corporation and Standing Committee to delegate their powers downward to subordinate officers for administrative efficiency.

title: Power of Central Government to make rules
text: (1) The Central Government, after consulting the Corporation and subject to previous publication, may make rules not inconsistent with the Act to give effect to its provisions.

sub_structure.2_ac: Rules may cover the manner of appointment/election of members of the Corporation, Standing Committee and Medical Benefit Council.
sub_structure.2_b_to_ei: Rules may cover meeting quorums, records of business, powers/duties/service conditions of the Director General and Financial Commissioner, Medical Benefit Council powers/duties, administrative-expense types and limits, contribution rates and wage thresholds, average-daily-wage calculation, recovery certificate procedures, funeral expense amounts, and the qualifications/conditions/rates/periods for sickness, maternity, disablement and dependants' benefits.
sub_structure.2_eg_eh_ehh: Rules may cover conditions for continued medical benefit for those permanently disabled out of employment, those who reach superannuation, and those who take voluntary or premature retirement.
sub_structure.2_ei_appeals: Rules may cover the manner and time for filing appeals to medical appeal tribunals or Employees' Insurance Courts.
sub_structure.2_f_to_o: Rules may cover contract execution procedure, property acquisition/holding/disposal, loan raising/repayment, fund investment, asset/liability valuation basis, banking arrangements, accounts and audit timing, publication of accounts/audit reports and recovery of disallowed items, budget preparation, and staff benefit funds.
sub_structure.2_oa: Rules may cover the period of cash-benefit non-entitlement following an insured person's conviction.
sub_structure.2_p: Rules may cover any other matter the Act allows/requires the Central Government to prescribe.
sub_structure.2A: Rule-making power includes power to give retrospective effect (not earlier than the Act's commencement), provided it does not prejudicially affect any person other than the Corporation.
sub_structure.3: Rules under this section, once published in the Official Gazette, have effect as if enacted in the Act.
sub_structure.4: Every rule must be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days (in one or more sessions); if both Houses agree to modify or annul it before the next session ends, the rule has effect only as modified, or ceases to have effect, without prejudice to anything previously done under it.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Central Government extensive rule-making power covering nearly every operational and benefit-related aspect of the scheme-from governance body procedures to contribution rates and benefit conditions-subject to Corporation consultation and parliamentary oversight.

title: Power of State Government to make rules
text: (1) The State Government, after consulting the Corporation and subject to previous publication, may make rules not inconsistent with the Act on matters including: (a) constitution and qualifications of Employees' Insurance Court Judges and their service conditions; (b) Court procedure and execution of Court orders; (c) application fees, litigation costs, and application form/particulars for the Court; (d) hospital/dispensary establishment and allotment of insured persons/families; (e) medical benefit scale, medical records and statistical returns; (ee) organisational structure/functions/powers/activities for a State-established medical organisation; (f) staff, equipment and medicine provision at hospitals/dispensaries; (g) service conditions of such institutional staff; and (h) any other State Government-prescribable matter.

sub_structure.2: Rules under this section, once published in the Official Gazette, have effect as if enacted in the Act.
sub_structure.3: Every rule must be laid before each House of the State Legislature (or the single House, where unicameral).

plain_english_summary: Gives State Governments rule-making power over the Employees' Insurance Court's constitution and procedure, and over State-level medical-benefit infrastructure and staffing.

title: Power of Corporation to make regulations
text: (1) The Corporation, subject to previous publication, may make regulations not inconsistent with the Act and rules, for administering its affairs and carrying the Act's provisions into effect.

sub_structure.2_i_to_v: Regulations may cover meeting times/places/procedure, factory/establishment registration timing and manner, matters referred by the Standing Committee to the Corporation, contribution assessment/collection manner, higher interest rates on delayed contributions, wage reckoning for contributions, the immediate employer's employee register, entitlement to sickness/temporary-disablement benefit on working/leave/strike days, and sickness certification/cash-benefit eligibility.
sub_structure.2_vi_to_xiv: Regulations may cover the method for determining occupational-disease status, valuing non-cash benefits, the timing/form/manner and particulars of benefit claims, circumstances for dismissing/punishing a disablement-benefit recipient, the manner/place/time of benefit payment, cash-benefit calculation and commutation methods, pregnancy/confinement/sickness notice and proof requirements (including maternity-benefit certifying authority, nomination for maternity benefit on death, and proof for maternity/additional maternity benefit), conditions for benefit suspension, and conditions/periodical medical examination for benefit recipients.
sub_structure.2_xvi_to_xxiii: Regulations may cover appointment, duties and certificate forms for medical practitioners, sickness-certifying qualifications, constitution of medical boards and appeal tribunals, penalties (wage-based fines) for employee breach of regulations, damages recoverable as penalty and sick-industrial-company waiver terms, regulation-relaxation circumstances and authority, employer returns/registers/records forms and timing, Social Security Officer and staff duties/powers, appellate authority constitution and interest on employer deposits, staff recruitment/pay/discipline/superannuation conditions (other than for the Director General/Financial Commissioner), contribution remittance procedure, and any other matter regulations are required/permitted to address.
sub_structure.2A: The previous-publication requirement does not apply to staff service-condition regulations under clause (xxi).
sub_structure.3: Regulations, once published in the Gazette of India, have effect as if enacted in the Act.
sub_structure.4: Every regulation must be forwarded to the Central Government, which lays it before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days (in one or more sessions); if both Houses agree to modify or annul it before the next session ends, the regulation has effect only as modified, or ceases to have effect, without prejudice to anything previously done under it.

plain_english_summary: Empowers the Corporation itself to make the most granular operational regulations-covering registration, contribution assessment, benefit claims and certification, medical boards, staff conditions, and penalties-subject to publication and parliamentary laying requirements.

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1951, with effect from its commencement. (Formerly allowed the Corporation to undertake duties in Part B States.)
plain_english_summary: This section, which previously addressed the Corporation's duties in former Part B States, has been omitted.

title: Medical care for the families of insured persons
text: At any time its funds permit, the Corporation may provide or contribute towards the cost of medical care for the families of insured persons.
plain_english_summary: Gives the Corporation discretionary power, funds permitting, to extend medical care support to insured persons' families.

title: Power to remove difficulties
text: (1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the Act's provisions, the Central Government may, by published order, make provisions or give directions, not inconsistent with the Act, as appear necessary or expedient to remove the difficulty.

sub_structure.2: Any such order has effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent in rules or regulations made under the Act.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Central Government a residual power to resolve implementation difficulties by order, overriding inconsistent rules or regulations if necessary.

title: Repeals and savings
text: If, immediately before the Act's commencement in a former Part B State area, a corresponding local law was in force, that law stands repealed on that day.

sub_structure.proviso1: The repeal does not affect the previous operation of such law, penalties/forfeitures/punishments already incurred, or related investigations/remedies, which may continue to be instituted, continued, enforced or imposed as if this Act had not been passed.
sub_structure.proviso2: Subject to the first proviso, anything done or action taken under the repealed law is deemed done or taken under the corresponding provision of this Act, and continues in force until superseded by action under this Act.

plain_english_summary: Repeals pre-existing corresponding State ESI-type laws upon this Act's commencement in those areas, while preserving past actions, liabilities and ongoing proceedings under the old law.

title: [Omitted]
text: Omitted by the Employees' State Insurance (Amendment) Act, 1989, with effect from 1-2-1991. (Formerly set out the manner of calculating average daily wages.)
plain_english_summary: This Schedule, which previously prescribed the method for calculating average daily wages, has been omitted; the calculation method is now prescribed by Central Government rules under section 42.

title: List of Injuries Deemed to Result in Permanent Disablement
text: Prescribed under section 2(15A) and (15B): Part I lists injuries deemed to result in permanent total disablement (100% loss of earning capacity), including loss of both hands, a hand and a foot, double leg/thigh amputation, sight loss preventing any eyesight-dependent work, very severe facial disfigurement, and absolute deafness. Part II lists injuries deemed to result in permanent partial disablement, with a specified percentage loss of earning capacity for each (ranging from upper- and lower-limb amputations at various levels, through loss of individual fingers/toes at various joints, to partial vision loss), with a note that complete and permanent loss of use of a listed limb/member is treated as equivalent to its loss.
plain_english_summary: A detailed medical injury-to-percentage table used to determine whether a workplace injury counts as permanent total disablement (automatic 100%) or permanent partial disablement (a specific percentage), directly feeding into disablement-benefit calculations.

title: List of Occupational Diseases
text: Prescribed under section 52A: Part A lists occupational diseases (e.g., infectious/parasitic diseases from lab, veterinary or animal-handling work; compressed-air diseases; lead, nitrous-fume, and organophosphorus poisoning) presumed work-related on exposure in specified employments. Part B lists diseases (e.g., caused by phosphorus, mercury, benzene, chromium, arsenic, radioactive substances, tar/pitch-related skin cancer, halogenated hydrocarbons, carbon disulphide, manganese, noise-induced hearing loss, beryllium, cadmium, occupational asthma, fluorine, nitro-glycerine, alcohols/ketones, asphyxiants, asbestos-related lung cancer/mesothelioma, and urinary-tract neoplasms) presumed work-related after at least six months' continuous exposure. Part C lists diseases (pneumoconioses/silicosis, bagassosis, byssinosis, extrinsic allergic alveolitis, hard-metal bronchopulmonary disease) presumed work-related after a Corporation-specified continuous exposure period.
plain_english_summary: Lists specific diseases linked to specific types of work, organised into three tiers by required exposure duration, which trigger the section 52A presumption that contracting the disease is a work-related 'employment injury' without needing to prove a specific accident.

title: Short title, extent and application
text: This Act may be called the Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. It extends to the whole of India except the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

sub_structure.3: (3) Subject to section 16, the Act applies to every factory engaged in a Schedule I industry employing 20 or more persons, and to any other establishment employing 20 or more persons (or class of establishments) that the Central Government notifies; the Central Government may also, after two months' notice, apply the Act to establishments with fewer than 20 employees.
sub_structure.4: (4) Even where an establishment does not otherwise cross the employee threshold, the Central Provident Fund Commissioner may apply the Act to it from the date of an agreement, if the employer and a majority of employees agree that the Act should apply.
sub_structure.5: (5) An establishment to which the Act applies continues to be governed by it even if its employee count later falls below twenty.

plain_english_summary: Names the Act, extends it across India (except Jammu and Kashmir, per the historical text), and fixes its coverage: factories in Schedule I industries and other notified establishments with 20 or more employees, with mechanisms to bring in smaller establishments by notification or mutual agreement, and a 'once covered, always covered' rule even if headcount later drops.

title: Definitions
text: In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires, the following terms have the meanings set out below.

sub_structure.a: "appropriate Government" means the Central Government for establishments belonging to or controlled by it, or connected with a railway, major port, mine, oilfield, controlled industry, or with departments/branches in more than one State; the State Government for all other establishments.
sub_structure.aa: "authorised officer" means the Central Provident Fund Commissioner or other specified Provident Fund Commissioners, or any officer authorised by the Central Government.
sub_structure.b: "basic wages" means all emoluments earned while on duty, leave or paid holidays under the employment contract and payable in cash, excluding food-concession value, dearness/house-rent/overtime allowances, bonus, commission or similar allowances, and employer presents.
sub_structure.e_f: "employer" means, for a factory, its owner/occupier or named manager; for other establishments, the person/authority with ultimate control, or its manager/managing director/managing agent. "employee" means any person employed for wages in connection with an establishment's work, including those employed through a contractor and certain apprentices (other than those under the Apprentices Act, 1961 or under standing orders).
sub_structure.ff_fff: "exempted employee" means an employee who but for an exemption under section 17 would have been covered by a Scheme/Insurance Scheme; "exempted establishment" means an establishment (or class/persons in it) granted such an exemption.
sub_structure.g_h_i: "factory" means premises where a manufacturing process is or is ordinarily carried on; "Fund" means the provident fund established under a Scheme; "industry" means an industry specified in Schedule I, or added to it by notification under section 4.
sub_structure.ia_ib: "Insurance Fund" means the Deposit-linked Insurance Fund under section 6C(2); "Insurance Scheme" means the Employees' Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme framed under section 6C(1).
sub_structure.j_k: "member" means a member of the Fund; "occupier of a factory" means the person with ultimate control over the factory's affairs, or a managing agent to whom those affairs are entrusted.
sub_structure.kA_kB: "Pension Fund" means the Employees' Pension Fund under section 6A(2); "Pension Scheme" means the Employees' Pension Scheme framed under section 6A(1).
sub_structure.ka_kb: "prescribed" means prescribed by rules under the Act; "Recovery Officer" means an officer of the Central/State Government or the Board of Trustees authorised by the Central Government to exercise recovery powers under the Act.
sub_structure.l_ll_m: "Scheme" means the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme under section 5; "Superannuation" for a Pension Scheme member means reaching age 58; "Tribunal" means the Industrial Tribunal referred to in section 7D.

plain_english_summary: Defines the Act's core vocabulary: who counts as an 'employer' and 'employee', what makes up 'basic wages' for contribution purposes, the various government-established funds and schemes (Provident Fund, Pension Fund, Insurance Fund/Scheme), and the officers (authorised officer, Recovery Officer) who administer and enforce the Act.

title: Establishment to include all departments and branches
text: For the removal of doubts, it is declared that where an establishment has different departments or branches, whether in the same place or different places, all such departments or branches are treated as parts of the same establishment.
plain_english_summary: Clarifies that an employer cannot avoid coverage by splitting a single business into separate departments or branch locations — they all count as one establishment.

title: Power to apply Act to an establishment which has a common provident fund with another establishment
text: Where, immediately before the Act becomes applicable to an establishment, a provident fund already exists that is common to employees of that establishment and another establishment, the Central Government may, by notification, direct that the Act shall also apply to that other establishment.
plain_english_summary: Lets the Central Government extend the Act to a second, linked establishment that already shares a common provident fund with a covered establishment, so both are brought under the same regime.

title: Power to add to Schedule I
text: The Central Government may, by notification, add any other industry to Schedule I if it believes a provident fund scheme should be framed for that industry's employees; the added industry is then treated as a Schedule I industry for the Act's purposes.

sub_structure.2: (2) All such notifications must be laid before Parliament as soon as possible after issue.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Central Government power to expand the list of industries covered by the Act simply by notification, subject to placing that notification before Parliament.

title: Employees' Provident Fund Schemes
text: The Central Government may, by notification, frame an Employees' Provident Fund Scheme for establishing provident funds for employees or classes of employees, specifying which establishments it applies to; a Fund must then be established in accordance with the Act and the Scheme.

sub_structure.1A: (1A) The Fund vests in, and is administered by, the Central Board constituted under section 5A.
sub_structure.1B: (1B) A Scheme may provide for any of the matters listed in Schedule II.
sub_structure.2: (2) A Scheme may take effect prospectively or retrospectively from a date specified in it.

plain_english_summary: Authorises the Central Government to create the Employees' Provident Fund Scheme itself — the main instrument that actually sets up and governs provident funds — and hands its administration to the Central Board.

title: Central Board
text: The Central Government may, by notification, constitute a Board of Trustees for all territories the Act extends to (the Central Board), consisting of a Chairman and Vice-Chairman, the Central Provident Fund Commissioner (ex officio), officials, State Government representatives, and equal numbers of employer and employee representatives appointed after consulting recognised organisations.

sub_structure.2: (2) Terms of appointment and meeting procedure for Central Board members are set out in the Scheme.
sub_structure.3_4: (3)-(4) The Central Board administers the vested Fund as specified in the Scheme, and performs other functions required by the Scheme, Pension Scheme and Insurance Scheme.
sub_structure.5_9: (5)-(9) The Central Board must keep proper accounts, subject to annual audit by the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India, and must submit an annual report and audited accounts to the Central Government for tabling before Parliament.

plain_english_summary: Sets up the Central Board of Trustees — a tripartite body of government, employer and employee representatives — to run the Employees' Provident Fund, subject to CAG audit and annual reporting to Parliament.

title: Executive Committee
text: The Central Government may, by notification, constitute an Executive Committee to assist the Central Board, consisting of a Chairman drawn from the Central Board, government officials, and employer/employee representatives elected by the Central Board, plus the Central Provident Fund Commissioner ex officio.

sub_structure.3: (3) Appointment/election terms and meeting procedure for the Executive Committee are as specified in the Scheme.

plain_english_summary: Creates a smaller Executive Committee, drawn from Central Board members, to help the Board handle its day-to-day functions more efficiently.

title: State Board
text: The Central Government may, after consulting a State Government, by notification, constitute a Board of Trustees for that State (the State Board), in the manner provided in the Scheme.

sub_structure.2: (2) A State Board exercises such powers and duties as the Central Government assigns to it from time to time.
sub_structure.3: (3) Appointment terms and meeting procedure for State Board members are set out in the Scheme.

plain_english_summary: Allows the Central Government to set up a State-level Board of Trustees to help administer the Fund within a particular State, exercising powers delegated to it by the Central Government.

title: Board of Trustees to be body corporate
text: Every Board of Trustees constituted under section 5A or 5B is a body corporate under the name specified in its constituting notification, with perpetual succession and a common seal, and may sue and be sued in that name.
plain_english_summary: Gives the Central and State Boards of Trustees full legal personality, so they can hold property, enter contracts, and sue or be sued in their own name.

title: Appointment of officers
text: The Central Government appoints a Central Provident Fund Commissioner as the Central Board's chief executive officer, subject to the Board's general control, and may appoint a Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer to assist him.

sub_structure.3: (3) The Central Board may appoint Additional/Deputy/Regional/Assistant Provident Fund Commissioners and other staff needed to run the Scheme, Pension Scheme and Insurance Scheme, within prescribed pay scales.
sub_structure.4: (4) Appointments to senior posts require prior consultation with the Union Public Service Commission, except for short (under one year) appointments or where the appointee is already an IAS officer or in Group A/B government service.
sub_structure.5: (5) A State Board may, with State Government approval, appoint necessary staff.
sub_structure.6_8: (6)-(8) Recruitment method, pay and service conditions for the Commissioner and other officers are fixed by the Central Government or Central Board (in line with comparable Central Government posts), and for State Board staff by that Board with State Government approval.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the administrative machinery of Provident Fund Commissioners and support staff who run the Fund day to day, with UPSC consultation required for senior appointments and pay/service conditions benchmarked to Central Government norms.

title: Acts and proceedings of the Central Board or its Executive Committee or the State Board not to be invalidated on certain grounds
text: No act or proceeding of the Central Board, its Executive Committee, or a State Board is invalid merely because of a vacancy in, or a defect in the constitution of, that body.
plain_english_summary: Protects decisions of the Central Board, Executive Committee, or State Boards from being challenged purely because of an unfilled seat or a technical flaw in how the body was set up.

title: Delegation
text: The Central Board may delegate powers/functions to its Executive Committee, its Chairman, or any of its officers; a State Board may delegate to its Chairman or officers, subject to conditions it specifies, as needed for efficient administration of the Scheme, Pension Scheme and Insurance Scheme.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Central and State Boards to hand off some of their powers to committees, chairpersons, or officers so the Fund can be run efficiently.

title: Contributions and matters which may be provided for in Schemes
text: The employer must pay to the Fund a contribution of ten per cent of each employee's basic wages, dearness allowance and retaining allowance (if any); the employee's matching contribution equals the employer's, though an employee may voluntarily contribute more, without obliging the employer to match the excess.

sub_structure.proviso_1: For establishments the Central Government specifies by notification, the ten per cent rate is raised to twelve per cent.
sub_structure.proviso_2: Where a contribution involves a fraction of a rupee, the Scheme may provide for rounding to the nearest rupee, half-rupee, or quarter-rupee.
sub_structure.explanation_1_2: "Dearness allowance" includes the cash value of any food concession; "retaining allowance" means an allowance paid to retain an employee's services during a period the establishment is not working.

plain_english_summary: Fixes the core funding mechanism of the Act: employer and employee each contribute a matching percentage (10%, or 12% for specified establishments) of basic wages plus dearness and retaining allowance to the Provident Fund.

title: Employees' Pension Scheme
text: The Central Government may, by notification, frame an Employees' Pension Scheme providing superannuation, retiring or permanent-total-disablement pension to employees, and widow/widower's, children's or orphan's pension to their beneficiaries.

sub_structure.2: (2) A Pension Fund is established, funded by a share of the employer's contribution (up to 8⅓% of basic wages/DA/retaining allowance), sums from exempted establishments, the transferred net assets of the earlier Family Pension Fund, and any Parliament-appropriated Central Government sums.
sub_structure.3: (3) On the Pension Fund's establishment, the earlier Family Pension Scheme ceases, and its assets/liabilities/beneficiary entitlements transfer to the Pension Fund (with benefits no less than before).
sub_structure.4_5: (4)-(5) The Pension Fund vests in and is administered by the Central Board, and the Pension Scheme may cover matters listed in Schedule III.
sub_structure.6_7: (6)-(7) The Pension Scheme may apply prospectively or retrospectively, and must be laid before Parliament for thirty days, with Parliament able to modify or annul it.

plain_english_summary: Creates the Employees' Pension Scheme, funded mainly by redirecting part of the employer's provident fund contribution, providing pensions to employees and their families on retirement, disability or death, replacing the earlier Family Pension Scheme.

title: Employees' Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme
text: The Central Government may, by notification, frame an Employees' Deposit-linked Insurance Scheme to provide life insurance benefits to employees of covered establishments.

sub_structure.2: (2) A Deposit-linked Insurance Fund is established, funded by employer contributions (up to a Central Government-specified percentage, not more than 1%, of basic wages/DA/retaining allowance).
sub_structure.4: (4) The employer must also pay administrative charges (up to one-fourth of the section 6C(2) contribution) to cover the Insurance Scheme's running costs.
sub_structure.5_7: (5)-(7) The Insurance Fund vests in and is administered by the Central Board; the Insurance Scheme may cover matters in Schedule IV, and may apply prospectively or retrospectively.

plain_english_summary: Sets up a life-insurance benefit for employees, funded entirely by employer contributions into a dedicated Deposit-linked Insurance Fund administered by the Central Board.

title: Laying of schemes before Parliament
text: Every scheme framed under section 5, 6A or 6C must be laid before each House of Parliament, as soon as possible after being framed, for a total of thirty days (in one or more sessions); if both Houses agree to modify or reject the scheme within that time, it takes effect only as modified, or not at all, without affecting anything already validly done under it.
plain_english_summary: Subjects the Provident Fund, Pension and Insurance Schemes to parliamentary scrutiny, giving Parliament thirty sitting days to modify or block a scheme after it is framed.

title: Modification of Scheme
text: The Central Government may, by notification, add to, amend, or vary (prospectively or retrospectively) the Scheme, Pension Scheme or Insurance Scheme.

sub_structure.2: (2) Every such notification must be laid before Parliament for thirty days, with Parliament able to modify or annul it, without prejudice to anything already done under it.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Central Government ongoing power to amend the Provident Fund, Pension, or Insurance Schemes by notification, subject to the same thirty-day parliamentary review process.

title: Determination of moneys due from employers
text: Specified Provident Fund Commissioners may, by order, decide disputes about whether the Act applies to an establishment, and determine amounts due from an employer under the Act, Scheme, Pension Scheme or Insurance Scheme, conducting whatever inquiry is necessary.

sub_structure.2: (2) For such inquiries, the officer has civil-court powers to summon and examine witnesses on oath, demand document production, receive affidavit evidence, and issue witness-examination commissions; the inquiry is deemed a judicial proceeding under the Indian Penal Code.
sub_structure.3: (3) No order can be made without giving the employer a reasonable opportunity to state their case.
sub_structure.3A: (3A) If a party fails, without valid reason, to attend the inquiry or produce documents, the officer may decide the matter based on the evidence and records available.
sub_structure.4: (4) An employer against whom an ex parte order was passed may, within three months, apply to have it set aside if they show the notice was not properly served or they had sufficient cause for non-appearance; this route is unavailable if an appeal against the ex parte order has already been decided (other than by withdrawal).
sub_structure.5: (5) No order can be set aside under sub-section (4) without notice to the opposite party.

plain_english_summary: Gives Provident Fund Commissioners quasi-judicial powers to hold inquiries, hear both sides, and formally determine both coverage disputes and the exact amount an employer owes under the Act's various schemes.

title: Review of orders passed under section 7A
text: A person aggrieved by a non-appealed section 7A order who discovers important new evidence, or identifies a mistake apparent on the record, or has other sufficient reason, may apply to the same officer for a review; the officer may also review the order on their own motion.

sub_structure.3_4: (3)-(4) The officer rejects the review application if there is no sufficient ground, or grants it after giving all parties notice and a hearing, with proof required for any 'new evidence' claim.
sub_structure.5: (5) No appeal lies against rejection of a review application, but an appeal lies against an order passed on review, as if it were an original section 7A order.

plain_english_summary: Creates a limited review mechanism for section 7A orders, allowing correction of genuine errors or newly discovered evidence, while channelling further challenges through the normal appeal route rather than repeated reviews.

title: Determination of escaped amount
text: If, after a section 7A or 7B order, the officer has reason to believe an amount escaped assessment — whether due to the employer's omission to disclose material facts, or otherwise, based on later information — the officer may, within five years of the earlier order, reopen the case and re-determine the correct amount due, after giving the employer a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
plain_english_summary: Lets the authorities revisit and correct a previous determination within five years if it turns out the employer's dues were understated, whether due to concealment or newly available information.

title: Tribunal
text: The Industrial Tribunal constituted by the Central Government under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, is, from the commencement of the relevant part of the Finance Act, 2017, the Tribunal for this Act's purposes, exercising the jurisdiction and powers this Act confers on it.
plain_english_summary: Designates the existing Industrial Tribunal (rather than a separate dedicated body) as the appellate Tribunal for Provident Fund Act matters, following the 2017 restructuring of government tribunals.

title: [Omitted] Term of office
text: This section, which dealt with the term of office of the Tribunal's Presiding Officer, was omitted by the Finance Act, 2017.
plain_english_summary: No longer operative; superseded by the 2017 restructuring that merged this Tribunal's functions into the existing Industrial Tribunal framework.

title: [Omitted] Resignation
text: This section, which dealt with resignation of the Tribunal's Presiding Officer, was omitted by the Finance Act, 2017.
plain_english_summary: No longer operative, for the same reason as section 7E.

title: [Omitted] Salary, allowances and conditions of service of Presiding Officer
text: This section, which dealt with the Presiding Officer's salary and service conditions, was omitted by the Finance Act, 2017.
plain_english_summary: No longer operative, for the same reason as section 7E.

title: [Omitted] Staff of Tribunal
text: This section, which dealt with the Tribunal's staff, was omitted by the Finance Act, 2017.
plain_english_summary: No longer operative, for the same reason as section 7E.

title: Appeals to Tribunal
text: A person aggrieved by a notification or order of the Central Government or an authority under section 1's proviso/(4), section 3, section 7A(1), section 7B (except review-rejection orders), section 7C, or section 14B, may appeal to a Tribunal.

sub_structure.2: (2) Every appeal must be filed in the prescribed form and manner, within the prescribed time, and with prescribed fees.

plain_english_summary: Gives employers and other aggrieved persons a formal right of appeal to the Tribunal against key coverage, assessment, and damages decisions made under the Act.

title: Procedure of Tribunals
text: A Tribunal regulates its own procedure, including where it sits.

sub_structure.2: (2) For discharging its functions the Tribunal has the same powers as officers under section 7A; its proceedings are deemed judicial proceedings under the Indian Penal Code, and it is deemed a civil court for certain purposes of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Tribunal flexibility over its own procedures while equipping it with the same investigative powers as the Commissioners whose orders it reviews.

title: Right of appellant to take assistance of legal practitioner and of Government, etc., to appoint presenting officers
text: A person appealing to a Tribunal may appear in person or engage a legal practitioner of their choice to present their case.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Central Government, a State Government, or any other authority under the Act may authorise legal practitioners or its own officers to act as presenting officers before the Tribunal.

plain_english_summary: Ensures appellants can be legally represented before the Tribunal, while also letting the government side appoint its own presenting officers or lawyers.

title: Orders of Tribunal
text: After hearing both parties, a Tribunal may confirm, modify or annul the order under appeal, or refer the case back to the original authority for fresh adjudication with directions, taking additional evidence if necessary.

sub_structure.2: (2) Within five years of its order, the Tribunal may correct any mistake apparent from the record, on its own motion or when a party points it out; an amendment increasing the employer's liability requires prior notice and a hearing.
sub_structure.3_4: (3)-(4) The Tribunal sends a copy of its order to the parties, and a final order disposing of an appeal cannot be questioned in any court.

plain_english_summary: Defines the Tribunal's powers on appeal — confirm, change, cancel, or remand a decision — with a limited window to fix clerical or record-based mistakes, and makes its final orders binding and not further challengeable in court.

title: [Omitted] Filling up of vacancies
text: This section, which dealt with filling vacancies in the Tribunal, was omitted by the Finance Act, 2017.
plain_english_summary: No longer operative, for the same reason as section 7E.

title: [Omitted] Finality of orders constituting a Tribunal
text: This section, which dealt with the finality of orders constituting the Tribunal, was omitted by the Finance Act, 2017.
plain_english_summary: No longer operative, for the same reason as section 7E.

title: Deposit of amount due, on filing appeal
text: A Tribunal cannot entertain an employer's appeal unless the employer has deposited seventy-five per cent of the amount determined as due under section 7A.

sub_structure.proviso: The Tribunal may, for recorded reasons, waive or reduce the deposit requirement.

plain_english_summary: Requires an employer to pay most of the disputed amount upfront before their appeal is even heard, though the Tribunal can relax this in appropriate cases.

title: Transfer of certain applications to Tribunals
text: All applications pending before the Central Government under the now-repealed section 19A stand transferred to the Tribunal with jurisdiction over the relevant establishments, treated as appeals to that Tribunal.
plain_english_summary: Handles the transitional housekeeping of moving old pending applications into the new Tribunal appeal system.

title: Interest payable by the employer
text: The employer is liable to pay simple interest at twelve per cent per annum (or a higher Scheme-specified rate) on any amount due under the Act, from the date it became due until actually paid.

sub_structure.proviso: Any higher rate specified in the Scheme cannot exceed the lending rate charged by a scheduled bank.

plain_english_summary: Imposes an automatic interest charge on any overdue amount an employer owes under the Act, to discourage late payment.

title: Mode of recovery of moneys due from employers
text: Amounts due from an employer in respect of contributions, damages recoverable under section 14B, accumulations to be transferred under sections 15/17, or other charges under the Act/Scheme/Insurance Scheme, may, if in arrears, be recovered in the manner specified in sections 8B to 8G.

sub_structure.b: (b) The same recovery route applies to an exempted establishment's employer for damages under section 14B, or charges payable to the appropriate Government under section 17's conditions, including Pension Scheme contributions.

plain_english_summary: Establishes that unpaid Provident Fund dues, damages, and related charges are recovered through the dedicated certificate-and-Recovery-Officer machinery set out in the following sections, similar to tax-recovery procedures.

title: Recovery of moneys by employers and contractors
text: Contribution amounts (employer's and employee's share, and Insurance Scheme employer contribution) and administrative charges paid or payable by an employer for a contractor's employee may be recovered by the employer from the contractor, by deduction from amounts owed to the contractor or as a debt.

sub_structure.2: (2) A contractor may, in turn, recover the employee's contribution from the employee by deduction from wages.
sub_structure.3: (3) A contractor cannot deduct or otherwise recover the employer's contribution or administrative charges from the employee's wages, despite any contrary contract.

plain_english_summary: Creates a pass-through chain for contract labour: the principal employer can claw back Provident Fund costs from the contractor, and the contractor can recover only the employee's own share from the worker — never the employer's share.

title: Issue of certificate to the Recovery Officer
text: Where an amount is in arrears, the authorised officer may issue a certificate to the Recovery Officer specifying the arrears; the Recovery Officer then recovers the amount by attaching and selling movable/immovable property, arresting and detaining the employer, or appointing a receiver to manage the establishment's or employer's property.

sub_structure.proviso: Attachment and sale must first target the establishment's own property; only if that is insufficient may the Recovery Officer proceed against the employer's personal property.
sub_structure.2: (2) A certificate may be issued even if other recovery modes are already underway.

plain_english_summary: Sets up a tax-recovery-style enforcement mechanism, letting authorities seize and sell property, or even detain a defaulting employer, to collect unpaid Provident Fund dues, targeting the business's assets before the employer's personal assets.

title: Recovery Officer to whom certificate is to be forwarded
text: The authorised officer forwards the recovery certificate to the Recovery Officer with jurisdiction over where the employer carries on business, or where the employer resides or has movable/immovable property.

sub_structure.2: (2) If property is spread across multiple jurisdictions and one Recovery Officer cannot recover the full amount, or expediency requires it, the certificate (or a certified copy for a partial amount) may also be sent to another Recovery Officer with jurisdiction over relevant property.

plain_english_summary: Ensures recovery certificates go to whichever Recovery Officer actually has jurisdiction over the employer's business or assets, and allows action across multiple jurisdictions if the defaulter's property is scattered.

title: Validity of certificate and amendment thereof
text: Once a certificate is issued, the employer cannot dispute the correctness of the amount, or raise any other objection, before the Recovery Officer.

sub_structure.2_3: (2)-(3) The authorised officer retains power to withdraw the certificate or correct clerical/arithmetical mistakes, and must inform the Recovery Officer of any such withdrawal, correction, or amendment.

plain_english_summary: Prevents the recovery certificate from being re-litigated at the enforcement stage, while still allowing the issuing officer to fix genuine clerical errors or withdraw the certificate if needed.

title: Stay of proceedings under certificate and amendment or withdrawal thereof
text: The authorised officer may grant the employer time to pay, causing the Recovery Officer to pause proceedings until that time expires.

sub_structure.2_3: (2)-(3) The authorised officer keeps the Recovery Officer informed of payments made or time extended, and must stay recovery of any reduced portion of the demand pending further appeal.
sub_structure.4: (4) Once an appeal is finally decided and the demand is reduced, the authorised officer amends or withdraws the certificate accordingly.

plain_english_summary: Builds flexibility into the recovery process so that payment plans, ongoing appeals, or reduced demands are properly reflected in what the Recovery Officer actually pursues.

title: Other modes of recovery
text: Besides the certificate route, the Central Provident Fund Commissioner or an authorised officer may recover arrears by requiring any person who owes money to the defaulting employer to instead pay that sum (up to the arrears) to the Commissioner, subject to normal court-attachment exemptions.

sub_structure.3: (3) A written garnishee-style notice may be issued to anyone holding or owing money to the employer, requiring payment to the Commissioner; recipients who falsely deny holding such money become personally liable if the denial is later shown false, and those who comply are discharged from liability to the employer to that extent.
sub_structure.4: (4) The Commissioner or authorised officer may apply to a court holding the employer's money for payment of the amount due.
sub_structure.5: (5) A sufficiently senior officer, if authorised, may recover arrears by distraint and sale of movable property, following Income-tax Act procedure.

plain_english_summary: Gives authorities alternative recovery tools beyond the certificate-to-Recovery-Officer route, including garnishee-style notices to third parties holding the employer's money and direct distraint of movable property.

title: Application of certain provisions of Income-tax Act
text: The Second and Third Schedules of the Income-tax Act, 1961, and the associated Certificate Proceedings Rules, apply with necessary modifications to recovering Provident Fund arrears as if they were income-tax dues, with "assessee" read as "employer".
plain_english_summary: Borrows the established Income-tax Act machinery for tax-recovery proceedings and applies it to Provident Fund arrears recovery, avoiding the need for a wholly separate procedure.

title: Fund to be recognised under Act 11 of 1922
text: For the purposes of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the Fund is deemed a recognised provident fund under Chapter IXA of that Act.

sub_structure.proviso: This deeming does not make ineffective any Scheme provision that conflicts with Chapter IXA or its rules.

plain_english_summary: Automatically gives the Provident Fund the tax-recognised status needed for its usual income-tax treatment, without a separate recognition process.

title: Protection against attachment
text: A member's (or exempted employee's) credit balance in the Fund cannot be assigned, charged, or attached under any court decree or order for the member's debts, and insolvency officials/receivers have no claim on it.

sub_structure.2: (2) On a member's death, the balance payable to a nominee vests in the nominee free of the deceased's or nominee's debts, and is also protected from court attachment.
sub_structure.3: (3) These protections extend equally to family pension or other Pension Scheme amounts, and to amounts payable under the Insurance Scheme.

plain_english_summary: Shields an employee's Provident Fund savings — and pension/insurance payouts — from being seized by creditors or claimed by an insolvency official, both during the member's life and after death when paid to a nominee.

title: Priority of payment of contributions over other debts
text: Where an employer is adjudicated insolvent or a winding-up order is made against a company, amounts due in respect of Fund/Insurance Fund contributions, section 14B damages, or transfer/charge obligations under the Act (accrued before the insolvency/winding-up order) are treated as debts entitled to priority payment under the Presidency-towns Insolvency Act, the Provincial Insolvency Act, or section 530 of the Companies Act, 1956.

sub_structure.explanation: "Insurance fund" here means any employer-established fund providing life-insurance-type benefits to employees, whether or not linked to their provident fund deposits.
sub_structure.2: (2) Separately, any amount due from an employer (whether the employee's deducted contribution or the employer's own contribution) is deemed a first charge on the establishment's assets and must be paid ahead of all other debts, notwithstanding any other law.

plain_english_summary: Puts unpaid Provident Fund contributions and related dues at the front of the queue when an employer becomes insolvent or a company is wound up, ranking them above most other creditors.
