sub_structure.2: (2) Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day (establishments up to 1,000 workmen) or 10th day (over 1,000) after the wage period ends.

plain_english_summary: Sets timelines for paying regular and unclaimed wages, mirroring the Payment of Wages Act's 7-day/10-day deadlines based on establishment size.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS NOT BEING INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Stoppage of work

sub_structure.1: (1) The employer may stop any section of the establishment without notice for reasons like fire, breakdown, power stoppage, epidemic, or civil commotion beyond their control.
sub_structure.2: (2) Affected workmen must be notified by notice-board; detention beyond 1 hour after stoppage entitles workmen to wages for the whole detention period (piece-rate workers use their average daily earning); detention under 1 hour is unpaid; no other compensation is due; short lay-offs are treated as compulsory leave (paid or unpaid); indefinite lay-offs may lead to termination with due notice or pay in lieu.
sub_structure.3: (3) Lay-off periods due to plant failure or curtailed production are treated as compulsory leave; indefinitely long lay-offs may end in termination with notice or pay.
sub_structure.4: (4) During a strike affecting a section, the employer may close that and related sections, with notice given to affected workmen before resumption.

plain_english_summary: Lets employers halt work without notice for events beyond their control, sets pay rules for workers detained during stoppages (paid after 1 hour, unpaid before), and covers lay-off and strike-related closure procedures.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS NOT BEING INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Termination of employment

sub_structure.1: (1) Terminating a permanent workman requires one month's notice (monthly-rated) or two weeks' notice (others), or pay in lieu.
sub_structure.2: (2) Temporary workmen, probationers and badlis get no notice or pay in lieu on termination, but a temporary workman's services cannot be terminated as punishment without a misconduct hearing under Standing Order 14.
sub_structure.3: (3) On termination, earned wages and other dues must be paid before the expiry of the second working day after termination.

plain_english_summary: Sets notice requirements for terminating permanent workmen (1 month or 2 weeks depending on pay basis), exempts temporary/probationary/badli workers from notice (except for punitive termination), and requires final dues within two working days.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS NOT BEING INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Disciplinary action for misconduct

sub_structure.1: (1) A workman may be fined up to 2% of a month's wages for specified acts/omissions notified with government approval under section 8 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936.
sub_structure.2: (2) A workman may be suspended up to 4 days at a time, or dismissed without notice or compensation, for proven misconduct.
sub_structure.3: (3) Misconduct includes: wilful insubordination or disobedience; theft, fraud or dishonesty; wilful damage to employer property; bribery; habitual unauthorised absence (or over 10 days); habitual late attendance; habitual breach of applicable law; riotous/disorderly behaviour or acts subversive of discipline; habitual negligence; repeated finable acts; and illegal strike action or incitement.
sub_structure.4a: (4)(a) A workman facing contemplated/pending disciplinary or criminal proceedings may be suspended in writing, with detailed reasons supplied within a week.
sub_structure.4b: (4)(b) Subsistence allowance during suspension: for departmental enquiries, half wages for the first 90 days, three-quarters beyond that (reduced to one-quarter if the delay is the workman's fault); for outside-agency enquiries or criminal proceedings, half wages for the first 180 days, three-quarters beyond that (similarly reduced if delay is the workman's fault).
sub_structure.4ba: (b-a) The workman may appear in person or be represented by a trade-union office-bearer during the enquiry.
sub_structure.4bb: (b-b) Enquiry proceedings shall be recorded in Hindi, English, or the local State language, per the workman's preference.
sub_structure.4bc: (b-c) The enquiry must be completed within three months, extendable for recorded reasons.
sub_structure.4c: (c) If found guilty after a hearing on the proposed penalty, the employer may order dismissal, suspension, fine, stoppage of increment, or reduction in rank, with specific back-pay/suspension-period rules depending on the outcome and any Article 311(2) Constitutional protections that apply.
sub_structure.4d: (d) If found not guilty, the workman is deemed on duty throughout the suspension and entitled to full wages minus the subsistence allowance already paid.
sub_structure.4e: (e) Subsistence allowance payment is conditional on the workman not taking other employment during suspension.
sub_structure.5: (5) Punishment decisions must consider the misconduct's gravity, the workman's prior record, and any extenuating or aggravating circumstances; a copy of the punishment order must be given to the workman.
sub_structure.6a: (6)(a) A workman aggrieved by a punishment order may appeal to the appellate authority within 21 days of receiving the order.
sub_structure.6b: (6)(b) The employer must specify who the appellate authority is.
sub_structure.6c: (6)(c) The appellate authority must hear the workman and decide the appeal within 15 days, communicating the decision in writing.

plain_english_summary: Provides the full misconduct and disciplinary framework: what counts as misconduct, fine/suspension/dismissal powers, detailed subsistence-allowance rules during suspension pending inquiry, enquiry procedure and timelines, back-pay rules depending on outcome, and a 21-day appeal right.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS NOT BEING INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Complaints
text: All employment-related complaints, including unfair treatment or wrongful exaction, shall be submitted to the manager or specified person, with a right of appeal to the employer.
plain_english_summary: Gives workers a complaint channel to the manager with a further appeal right to the employer.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS NOT BEING INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Certificate on termination of service
text: Every permanent workman is entitled to a service certificate on dismissal, discharge or retirement.
plain_english_summary: Guarantees a permanent workman a service certificate whenever their employment ends.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS NOT BEING INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Liability of employer
text: The employer of the establishment is personally responsible for the proper and faithful observance of the standing orders.
plain_english_summary: Makes the employer personally accountable for ensuring the standing orders are actually followed.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS NOT BEING INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Appeal procedure (duplicate of Rule 7-A)
text: Sets out the same appeal procedure as Rule 7-A: memorandum of appeal in quintuplicate with certified copy of the standing orders, hearing by the appellate authority, notice to affected parties, and evidence-taking at the hearing.
plain_english_summary: Restates the standing-orders appeal procedure (memorandum of appeal, hearing, notice to parties) within the Model Standing Orders themselves.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS NOT BEING INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Exhibition of standing orders
text: A copy of these orders in English and Hindi shall be posted on a notice-board at or near the main entrance and kept legible.
plain_english_summary: Requires the standing orders themselves to be permanently and legibly displayed in English and Hindi at the establishment's entrance.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Commencement
text: These orders shall come into force on the date specified.
plain_english_summary: States that the coal-mine standing orders take effect from a specified date.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Definitions

sub_structure.a: (a) 'attendance' means presence at the required place for work with attendance marked.
sub_structure.b: (b) 'employer' and 'workman' carry the meanings in sections 2(d) and 2(i) of the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946.
sub_structure.c: (c) 'Manager' means the mine's manager, including an acting manager appointed under the Mines Act, 1952.
sub_structure.d: (d) Masculine words include females.
sub_structure.e: (e) Singular includes plural and vice versa.

plain_english_summary: Defines attendance, employer/workman (by cross-reference to the parent Act), manager, and standard gender/number interpretation rules for the coal mine standing orders.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Classification of workmen

sub_structure.a: (a) Workmen are classified as: permanent, probationers, badlis/substitutes, temporary, apprentices, and casual.
sub_structure.b: (b) A 'permanent workman' is appointed for an unlimited period or has completed 3 months' continuous service as a probationer in a permanent post.
sub_structure.c: (c) A 'probationer' provisionally fills a permanent vacancy and has under 3 months' service in that post (extendable); a permanent workman made probationer in a new post may revert during probation.
sub_structure.d: (d) A 'badli/substitute' fills in for a temporarily absent permanent workman/probationer, ceasing to be a badli after one year's continuous service (190 attendances below ground, 240 otherwise) in the same/similar post, or becoming permanent after completing a probationer's term.
sub_structure.e: (e) A 'temporary' workman is engaged for essentially temporary work with a specified (extendable) likely finish period.
sub_structure.f: (f) An 'apprentice' is a learner, paid or unpaid, per their training contract terms.
sub_structure.g: (g) A 'casual' workman is engaged for essentially casual work.

plain_english_summary: Defines six coal-mine worker categories, with badli status converting to permanent after specified continuous service thresholds (190/240 attendances or one year).

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Tickets
text: Every workman is given a classification-appropriate ticket at appointment, bearing their signature/thumb-impression, shown to authorised persons on request; a lost ticket is replaced for 25 paisa.
plain_english_summary: Requires signed/thumb-printed identity tickets for every coal-mine worker, replaceable for a small fee if lost.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Display of notices
text: Shift periods/hours, holidays, pay-days, and wage rates/allowance scales shall be displayed in English and the majority local language on notice-boards at the main entrance and time-keeper's office.
plain_english_summary: Requires bilingual posting of shift hours, holidays, pay-days, and wage rates at the mine entrance and time-keeper's office.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Payment of wages

sub_structure.a: (a) Wages are paid directly to workmen on a working day between 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. at the mine office, witnessed and attested by the manager or an authorised person; contractor's workmen are paid at a manager-specified place, witnessed by an employer's nominee.
sub_structure.b: (b) Unclaimed wages are paid on a notified weekly unclaimed-wage day, or remitted by money order (minus commission) on request, with claims presentable within 12 months of falling due.
sub_structure.c: (c) Overtime is worked and paid per the Mines Act, 1952 (as amended); weekly-rest-day work is paid per agreement, award, usage or custom.

plain_english_summary: Sets wage payment timing, witnessing/attestation requirements, unclaimed-wage handling, and overtime pay rules tied to the Mines Act.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Shift working
text: Mirrors the general Schedule I shift-working rule: multiple shifts allowed at employer discretion with worker transfer liability; two months' notice needed to discontinue a shift (unless by agreement); retrenchment/re-employment from shift changes follows the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.
plain_english_summary: Applies the same multi-shift and two-month-notice framework as the general standing orders, tied to Industrial Disputes Act compliance for related retrenchment.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Attendance
text: All workmen must be at work at the mine at the fixed, notified time.
plain_english_summary: Requires punctual attendance at the mine.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Absence from place of work
text: A workman found absent from their proper work post during working hours without permission or sufficient reason is treated as absent for that period.
plain_english_summary: Treats unauthorised absence from one's post (even while technically at the mine) as absence for pay purposes.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Festival holidays and leave

sub_structure.a: (a) Seven paid festival holidays apply (Republic Day, Independence Day, and Gandhi's Birthday mandatory; the rest by agreement/local custom); working on a holiday earns triple pay, or double pay plus a substituted paid holiday.
sub_structure.b1: (b)(i) Leave with wages follows Chapter VII of the Mines Act, 1952.
sub_structure.b2: (b)(ii) Leave applied for is normally granted, though the employer may refuse/revoke/curtail it for work exigencies, with wages in lieu paid where refused or unaccumulable, and a railway-concession makeup mechanism if leave is refused one year.
sub_structure.c: (c) Quarantine leave is granted (on a medical certificate) for contagious-disease exposure through no fault of the worker, paid at 50% of wages, unless the worker previously refused prophylactic treatment.
sub_structure.d: (d) Leave applications must be made at least 15 days ahead (except unforeseen circumstances), decided within a week (or by two days before leave start, whichever is earlier, or same-day if leave starts within 3 days), with refusals/postponements and reasons recorded in writing.
sub_structure.e: (e) Overstaying leave beyond 10 days without satisfactory explanation causes loss of job lien, placing the worker on the badli list.
sub_structure.f: (f) Casual leave with pay is capped at 5 days a year, max 3 consecutive days except for sickness, requiring prior (or prompt written) notice.
sub_structure.g: (g) Overstaying sanctioned leave or unreasonable absence renders the workman liable to disciplinary action.

plain_english_summary: Sets holiday pay, general and quarantine leave, casual leave (5-day annual cap), leave-application timelines, and consequences for overstaying leave, specific to coal-mine conditions.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Medical aid in case of accident
text: Where a workman is injured in the course of employment, the employer must arrange immediate free medical aid and prompt payment of Workmen's Compensation Act benefits, covering the first three days of absence too.
plain_english_summary: Obliges the mine to provide free emergency medical care and prompt compensation for work injuries, including the initial three-day absence period.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Railway travel facilities

sub_structure.a: (a) A qualified workman proceeding on leave gets the equivalent cost of ticket/bus/boat fare home.
sub_structure.b: (b) Workers completing 12 months' continuous service (240+ days in the preceding 12 months) qualify for travel fare home and back.
sub_structure.c: (c) A returning workman gets a cash payment equal to the return fare; if the mine cannot re-engage him, the return fare is paid immediately.
sub_structure.d: (d) Mixed bus/train journeys are cost-adjusted accordingly.
sub_structure.e: (e) Entitlement is for mail/express train travel where tickets are available.
sub_structure.f: (f) Travel class depends on basic wage: Class III (up to Rs. 165/month), Class II (Rs. 165-265), Class I (above Rs. 265).

plain_english_summary: Provides home-leave travel reimbursement for qualified coal-mine workers, with the class of travel tied to the worker's basic wage.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Termination of services

sub_structure.a: (a) Permanent workmen with under a year's continuous service get one month's written notice (with reasons) or pay in lieu, except where terminated for established misconduct.
sub_structure.b: (b) Temporary and badli workmen generally need no termination notice, except temporary workmen with 3+ months' service get two weeks' notice if termination isn't per their contract terms; those with under 3 months' service, or terminated badlis, get written reasons instead.
sub_structure.c: (c) A workman resigning must give one month's (monthly-paid) or two weeks' (weekly-paid) written notice, though the employer may waive this for pay in lieu.
sub_structure.d: (d) 'Service' and 'wages' here carry the meanings from the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 sections 25(B)(1) and 2(rr).

plain_english_summary: Sets notice requirements for terminating or resigning from coal-mine employment, varying by worker category and length of service, cross-referencing Industrial Disputes Act definitions.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Stoppage of work and re-opening

sub_structure.a: (a) Subject to Chapter V-A of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, the employer may stop mine sections for reasons like underground trouble, fire, breakdown, epidemic or civil commotion beyond their control.
sub_structure.b: (b) Affected workmen are notified by notice-board; not ordinarily detained beyond 2 hours; lay-off compensation follows the Industrial Disputes Act where applicable, otherwise paid/unpaid leave applies; indefinitely long lay-offs may end in termination under that Act; resuming work requires two weeks' notice, with laid-off workers given re-employment preference.
sub_structure.c: (c) During a strike affecting a section, the employer may close that and related sections, with notice posted and sent to any registered trade union.

plain_english_summary: Allows temporary mine-section shutdowns for events beyond the employer's control, sets lay-off compensation and re-employment preference rules under the Industrial Disputes Act, and covers strike-related closures.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Method of filling vacancies
text: Badli and temporary workmen and probationers get seniority-based preference when filling permanent vacancies.
plain_english_summary: Gives existing badli, temporary and probationary workers seniority-based priority for permanent vacancies.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Transfers
text: Workmen may be transferred between departments, stations, or mines under the same ownership for work exigencies, provided pay, grade, continuity and conditions aren't adversely affected, the new job is similar and suitable, reasonable notice is given, and reasonable joining time is allowed for inter-station transfers; the worker is paid actual transport charges plus 50% for incidentals.
plain_english_summary: Permits transfers within the same ownership under conditions protecting pay/grade/continuity, with notice, joining time, and a transport-cost allowance.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Disciplinary action for misconduct

sub_structure.i: (i) A workman found guilty of misconduct may be suspended (without-pay suspension capped at 10 days), fined, have increment stopped, be demoted, or dismissed without notice; pending departmental enquiry, subsistence allowance is half wages up to 30 days, three-quarters beyond 30 days (or one-quarter if the delay is the workman's fault), conditional on not taking other employment, with enquiries normally completed within 10 days.
sub_structure.misconduct_list: Misconduct includes: theft/fraud/dishonesty; bribery; wilful insubordination; habitual late attendance/unauthorised absence; drunkenness or disorderly behaviour on duty; habitual work neglect or indiscipline; smoking underground where prohibited; wilful damage to work/property; sleeping on duty; malingering; accepting gifts from subordinates; criminal conviction involving moral turpitude; prolonged unauthorised absence (10+ days); false personal information at hiring; leaving work without permission; breaching the Mines Act or related rules/standing orders; threatening/assaulting superiors or co-workers; habitual money-lending; inciting violence; abetting misconduct; illegal strike without 14 days' notice; disclosing confidential information; refusing a charge-sheet/order/notice; and refusing to wear/use provided protective equipment.
sub_structure.ii: (ii) No punishment may be imposed without written notice of the alleged misconduct, an opportunity to explain, and a departmental enquiry (during which the workman may be suspended and may have a co-worker's assistance); dismissal requires the owner/agent/Chief Mining Engineer's approval; enquiry proceedings are shared with the workman on request.
sub_structure.iii: (iii) A workman not found guilty is deemed on duty throughout suspension and entitled to full wages.
sub_structure.iv: (iv) Punishment decisions must weigh the misconduct's gravity, prior record, and any extenuating/aggravating circumstances, with a copy of the order given to the workman.

plain_english_summary: Sets out coal-mine misconduct categories (a long list including safety, honesty, and discipline violations), disciplinary powers and subsistence-allowance rules during suspension, enquiry procedure with management-level sign-off for dismissal, and back-pay if exonerated.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Time-limit for making complaints, appeals, etc.
text: Employment-related complaints (including unfair treatment) must be submitted to the mine manager within 7 days of the cause of complaint, with a right of appeal to the employer within 3 days of the manager's decision; the employer normally decides the appeal within 3 days of receipt.
plain_english_summary: Sets tight timelines (7 days to complain, 3 days to appeal, 3 days for the employer to decide) for the coal-mine complaints process.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Liability of manager of the mine
text: The mine manager is personally responsible for proper enforcement of these standing orders, but where a manager is overruled by a superior, the superior bears responsibility for that decision.
plain_english_summary: Places enforcement responsibility on the mine manager personally, shifting it to a superior only where the manager's decision was overruled.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Service certificate
text: Every workman employed continuously for more than three months is entitled to a service certificate on leaving employment.
plain_english_summary: Guarantees a service certificate to any coal-mine worker with more than three months' continuous service upon leaving.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Entry and exit
text: Workmen must use authorised gates to enter/leave the premises and are liable to search; women workmen may only be searched by women.
plain_english_summary: Requires use of authorised entry/exit points and permits searches, with women searched only by women.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS FOR INDUSTRIAL ESTABLISHMENTS IN COAL MINES
title: Exhibition and supply of Standing Orders
text: A copy of these orders in English and the local regional language shall be posted at the manager's office and other mine locations, kept legible; a copy is supplied to a workman on request for a reasonable price, free to a recognised trade union.
plain_english_summary: Requires public, legible display of the standing orders and makes copies available to workers (for a fee) and recognised unions (free).

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS ON ADDITIONAL ITEMS APPLICABLE TO ALL INDUSTRIES
title: Service Record

sub_structure.i: (i) Service Card: every establishment must maintain a service card per workman, recorded with the workman's knowledge and attested by an authorised officer with date.
sub_structure.ii: (ii) Certification of service: every workman is entitled to a service certificate stating designation and employment period at discharge, termination, retirement or resignation.
sub_structure.iii: (iii) Residential address: a workman must notify the employer of their address on engagement and any subsequent change; the last known address is used otherwise.
sub_structure.iv: (iv) Record of age: a workman must state their date of birth at joining, supported by a matriculation/school certificate, a municipal/Panchayat/Registrar birth record, a Government Medical Officer's age certificate (at employer's cost if needed), or, failing those, a sworn affidavit; once entered in the service card (finalised within 3 months of appointment), the date of birth is sole evidence of age for all service purposes including retirement, and cases already settled before these provisions took effect are not reopened.

plain_english_summary: Establishes a mandatory service-card system recording verified date of birth (via a hierarchy of acceptable proofs), residential address, and service history, with the recorded birth date treated as conclusive for retirement and other purposes.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS ON ADDITIONAL ITEMS APPLICABLE TO ALL INDUSTRIES
title: Confirmation
text: The employer must confirm an eligible workman per their appointment letter's terms, issue a confirmation letter, and record the confirmation in the service card within 30 days.
plain_english_summary: Requires formal, documented confirmation of probationary workers into permanent status per their appointment terms.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS ON ADDITIONAL ITEMS APPLICABLE TO ALL INDUSTRIES
title: Age of retirement
text: Retirement age follows any agreement, settlement or award binding on employer and workman; absent such agreement, retirement is at 58 years.
plain_english_summary: Sets a default retirement age of 58 unless a binding agreement or award specifies otherwise.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS ON ADDITIONAL ITEMS APPLICABLE TO ALL INDUSTRIES
title: Transfer
text: A workman may be transferred between shops/departments/stations/establishments under the same employer for work exigencies, provided wages/grade/continuity/conditions aren't adversely affected, the new job is suitable, inter-state transfers require consent or a specific appointment-letter provision, and reasonable notice and joining time are given; the worker receives transport charges plus 50% for incidental expenses.
plain_english_summary: Permits transfers (including inter-state, with added consent safeguards) under the same conditions of pay/grade protection, notice, and a travel-cost allowance seen elsewhere in these rules.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS ON ADDITIONAL ITEMS APPLICABLE TO ALL INDUSTRIES
title: Medical aid in case of accidents
text: Where a workman is injured in the course of or arising from employment, the employer must, at their own expense, arrange immediate necessary medical aid and further treatment if the attending doctor considers it necessary, with ESI Act or Workmen's Compensation Act benefits and treatment arranged where the worker is entitled to them.
plain_english_summary: Requires employer-funded emergency and follow-up medical care for workplace injuries, coordinated with ESI Act or Workmen's Compensation Act entitlements.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS ON ADDITIONAL ITEMS APPLICABLE TO ALL INDUSTRIES
title: Medical examination
text: Where recruitment rules require a medical examination on first appointment, the employer must arrange it, at the employer's expense, through a registered medical practitioner.
plain_english_summary: Makes the employer responsible for arranging and paying for any pre-employment medical exam required by recruitment rules.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS ON ADDITIONAL ITEMS APPLICABLE TO ALL INDUSTRIES
title: Secrecy
text: A workman may not remove establishment papers/documents/property without written permission from their immediate superior, nor disclose manufacturing processes, trade secrets or confidential documents to unauthorised persons without the employer's written permission.
plain_english_summary: Imposes confidentiality obligations barring unauthorised removal or disclosure of company documents and trade secrets.

chapter_title: MODEL STANDING ORDERS ON ADDITIONAL ITEMS APPLICABLE TO ALL INDUSTRIES
title: Exclusive service
text: A workman must not work against the establishment's interests at any time, and must not take additional employment that could adversely affect the employer's interests.
plain_english_summary: Requires loyalty to the employer, barring outside work or actions that could harm the establishment's interests.

title: Short title, extent, commencement and application

sub_structure.1: (1) This Act may be called the Inter -State Migrant Workmen (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1979.
sub_structure.2: (2) It extends to the whole of India.
sub_structure.3: (3) It shall come into force on such date 1 as the Central Government may, by notification i n the Official Gazette, appoint: Provided that if the Central Government considers it necessary or expedient so to do in the public interest, it may postpone or relax, to such extent as may be specified in s uch notification, the operation of all or any of the provisions of this Act in any State or States for such period not extending beyond one year from the date on which this Act comes into force.
sub_structure.4: (4) It applies— (a) to every establishment in which five or m ore inter-State migrant workmen (whether or not in addition to other workmen) are employed or who were employed on any day of the preceding twelve months; (b) to every contractor who employs or who employed five or more inter -State migrant workmen (whether or not in addition to other workmen) on any day of the preceding twelve months.

plain_english_summary: Names the Act, extends it to all of India, allows the Central Government to notify commencement dates (with an option to apply it immediately in urgent public-interest cases), and applies it to establishments/contractors engaging five or more inter-State migrant workmen.

title: Definitions

sub_structure.1: (1) any establishment pertaining to any industry carried on by or under the authority of the Central Government or pertaining to any such controlled industry as may be specified in this behalf by the Central Government; or
sub_structure.2: (2) Any reference in this Act to any law which is not in force in any area shall, in relation to that area, be construed as a reference to the corresponding law, if any, in force in that area. CHAPTER II REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
sub_structure.3: (3) any establishment of a banking or insurance company, the Central Government; (ii) in relation to any other establishment, the Government of the State in which that other establishment is situated; (b) “contractor”, in relation to an establishment, means a person who undertakes (whether as an independent contractor, agent, employee or otherwise) to produce a given result for the establishment, other than mere supply of goods or articles of manufacture to such establishment, by the employment of workmen or to supply workmen to the establishment, and includes a sub -contractor, Khatadar, Sardar, agent or any other person, by whatever name called, who recruits or employs workmen; (c) “controlled industry” means any industry the control of which by the Union has been declared by any Central Act to be expedient in the public interest; 1. 2nd October, 1980, vide notification No. G.S.R. 513(E), dated 11th August, 1980, see Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, sec. 3(i). (d) “establishment” means— (i) any office or department of the Government or a local authority; or (ii) any place where any industry, trade, business, manufacture or occupation is carried on; (e) “inter-State migrant workman” means any person who is recruited by or through a contractor in one State under an agreement or other arrangement for employment in an establishment in another State, whether with or without the knowledge of the principal employer in relation to such establishment; (f) “prescribed” means prescribed by rules made under this Act; (g) “principal employer” means,— (i) in relation to any offic e or department of the Government or a local authority, the head of that office, department or authority or such other officer as the Government or the local authority, as the case may be, may specify in this behalf; (ii) in relation to a factory, the owne r or occupier of the factory and where a person has been named as the manager of the factory under the Factories Act, 1948 (63 of 1948), the person so named; (iii) in relation to a mine, the owner or agent of the mine and where a person has been named as the manager of the mine, the person so named; (iv) in relation to any other establishment, any person responsible for the supervision and control of the establishment. Explanation.—For the purposes of sub -clause ( iii) of this clause, the expressions “mine”, “owner” and “agent” shall have the meanings respectively assigned to them in clause ( j), clause ( l) and clause (c) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Mines Act,1952 (35 of 1952); (h) “recruitment” includes entering into any agreement or other arrange ment for recruitment and all its grammatical variations and cognate expressions shall be construed accordingly; (i) “wages” shall have the meaning assigned to it in clause ( vi) of section 2 of the Payment of Wages Act, 1936 (4 of 1936); (j) “workman” means any person employed in or in connection with the work of any establishment to do any skilled, semi -skilled or unskilled, manual, supervisory, technical or clerical work for hire or reward, whether the terms of employment be express or implied, but does not include any such person— (i) who is employed mainly in a managerial or administration capacity; or (ii) who, being employed in a supervisory capacity, draws wages exceeding five hundred rupees per mensem, or exercises, either by the nature of the duties attached to the office or by reason of the powers vested in him, functions mainly of a managerial nature.

plain_english_summary: Defines the 'appropriate Government' (Central or State, depending on the establishment), 'contractor', and other key terms, and clarifies how references to laws not in force in an area should be construed.

chapter_title: REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Appointment of registering officers
text: The appropriate Government may, by order notified in the Official Gazette,— (a) appoint such persons, being officers of Government, as it thinks fit to be registering officers for the purposes of this Chapter; and (b) define the limits, within which a registering officer shall exercise the powers conferred on him by or under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Allows the appropriate Government to appoint registering officers (with defined territorial jurisdiction) to administer establishment registration under the Act.

chapter_title: REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Registration of certain establishments

sub_structure.1: (1) Every principal employer of an establishment to which this Act applies shall, within such period as the appropriate Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, fix in this behalf with respect to establishments generally or with respect to any class of them, make an application to the registering officer, in such form and manner and on payment of such fees as may be prescribed, for the registration of the establishment: Provided that the registerin g officer may entertain any such application for registration after the expiry of the period fixed in that behalf, if the registering officer is satisfied that the applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from making the application in time.
sub_structure.2: (2) Within one month after the receipt of an application for registration under sub -section (1), the registering officer shall,— (a) if the application is complete in all respects, register the establishment and issue to the principal employer of the establishment a certificate of registration in the prescribed form; and (b) if the application is not so complete, return the application to the principal employer of the establishment.
sub_structure.3: (3) Where within a period of one month after the receipt of an application for registration of an establishment under sub -section (1), the r egistering officer does not grant under clause (a) of sub-section (2) the certificate of registration applied for and does not return the application under clause (b) of that sub -section, the registering officer shall, within fifteen days of the receipt of an application in this behalf, from the principal employer, register the establishment and issue to the principal employer a certificate of registration in the prescribed form.

plain_english_summary: Requires principal employers to apply for registration of their establishment, sets a one-month timeline for the registering officer to grant or refuse a certificate, and treats non-response within that time as deemed registration.

chapter_title: REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Revocation of registration in certain cases
text: If the registering officer is satisfied, either on a reference made to him in this behalf or otherwise, that the registration of any establishment has been obtained by misrepresentation or suppr ession of any material fact or that for any other reason, the registration has become useless or ineffective and, therefore, requires to be revoked, the registering officer may, after giving an opportunity to the principal employer of the establishment to be heard and with the previous approval of the appropriate Government, revoke by order in writing the registration and communicate the order to the principal employer: Provided that where the registering officer considers it necessary so to do for any special reasons, he may, pending such revocation, by order suspend the operation of the certificate of registration for such period as may be specified in the order and serve, by registered post, such order along with a statement of the reasons on the principal employer and such order shall take effect on the date on which such service is effected.
plain_english_summary: Allows a registering officer to revoke an establishment's registration if it was obtained by misrepresentation or has become useless/ineffective, after giving the employer an opportunity to be heard.

chapter_title: REGISTRATION OF ESTABLISHMENTS EMPLOYING INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Prohibition against employment of inter-State migrant workmen without registration
text: No principal employer of an establishment to which this Act applies shall employ inter -State migrant workmen in the establishment unless a certificate of registration in respect of such establishment issued under this Act is in force: Provided that nothin g in this section shall apply to any establishment in respect of which an application for registration made within the period fixed, whether originally or on extension under sub-section (1) of section 4 is pending before a registering office r and for the purposes of this proviso, an application to which the provisions of sub -section (3) of section 4 apply shall be deemed to be pending before the registering officer concerned till the certificate of registration is issued in accordance with th e provisions of that sub-section. CHAPTER III LICENSING OF CONTRACTORS
plain_english_summary: Bars a principal employer from employing inter-State migrant workmen unless the establishment holds a valid registration certificate, with a limited exception while a registration application is pending.

title: Appointment of licensing officers
text: The appropriate Government may, by order not ified in the Official Gazette,— (a) appoint such persons, being officers of Government, as it thinks fit to be licensing officers for the purposes of this Chapter; and (b) define the limits, within which a licensing officer shall exercise the jurisdiction and powers conferred on licensing officers by or under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Allows the appropriate Government to appoint licensing officers (with defined jurisdiction) to administer contractor licensing under the Act.

title: Licensing of contractors

sub_structure.1: (1) With effect from such date as the appropriate Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, no contractor to whom this Act applies shall,— (a) recruit any person in a State for the purpose of employing him in any establishment situated in another State, except under and in accordance with a licence issued in that behalf— (i) if such establishment is an establishment referred to in sub -clause ( i) of clause ( a) of sub-section (1) of section 2, by the licensing officer appointed by the Central Government who has jurisdiction in relation to the area wherein the recruitment is made; (ii) if such establishment is an establishment referred to i n sub -clause ( ii) of clause ( a) of sub-section (1) of section 2, by the licensing officer appointed by the State Government who has jurisdiction in relation to the area wherein the recruitment is made; (b) employ as workmen for the exec ution of any work in any establishment in any State, persons from another State (whether or not in addition to other workmen) except under and in accordance with a licence issued in that behalf,— (i) if such establishment is an establishment referred to in sub-clause ( i) of clause ( a) of sub-section (1) of section 2, by the licensing officer appointed by the Central Government who has jurisdiction in relation to the area wherein the establishment is situated; (ii) if such establishm ent is an establishment referred to in sub -clause (ii) of clause ( a) of sub-section (1) of section 2, by the licensing officer appointed by the State Government who has jurisdiction in relation to the area wherein the establishment is situated.
sub_structure.2: (2) Subject to the provisions of this Act, a licence under sub -section (1) may contain such conditions including, in particular, the terms and conditions of the agreement or other arrangement under which the workmen will be recruited, the remuneration payable, hours of work, fixation of wages and other essential amenities in respect of the inter -State migrant workmen, as the appropriate Government may deem fit to impose in accordance with the rules, if any , made under section 35 and shall b e issued on payment of such fees as may be prescribed: Provided that if for any special reasons, the licensing officer is satisfied that it is necessary to require any person who has applied for, or who has been i ssued, a licence to furnish any security for the due performance of the conditions of the licence, he may, after communicating such reasons to such person and giving him an opportunity to represent his case, determine in accordance with the rules made in this behalf the security which shall be furn ished by such person for obtaining or, as the case may be, for continuing to hold the licence.
sub_structure.3: (3) The security which may be required to be furnished under the proviso to sub -section (2) shall be reasonable and the rules for the purposes of the said proviso shall, on the basis of the number of workmen employed, the wages payable to them, the facilities which shall be afforded to them and other relevant factors provide for the norms with reference to which such security may be determined.

plain_english_summary: Requires contractors to hold a licence before recruiting or employing inter-State migrant workmen, allows licence conditions (including a security deposit), and lets licences be issued for one or more States.

title: Grant of licences

sub_structure.1: (1) Every application for the grant of a licence under sub -section ( 1) of section 8 shall be made in the prescribed form and shall contain the particulars regarding the location of the establishment, the nature of process, operation or work for which inter-State migrant workmen are to be employed and such other particulars as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.2: (2) The licensing officer may make such investigation in respect of the application received under sub-section (1) and in making any such investigation, the lic ensing officer shall follow such procedure as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.3: (3) A licence granted under section 8, shall be valid for the period specified therein and may be renewed from time to time for such period and on payment of such fees and on such conditions as may be prescribed.

plain_english_summary: Sets the application process for a contractor's licence, allows the licensing officer to investigate applications, and specifies that licences are valid for a fixed period and may be renewed on payment of fees.

title: Revocation, suspension and amendment of licences

sub_structure.1: (1) If the licensing officer is satisfied, either on a reference made to him in this behalf or otherwise, that— (a) a licence granted under section 8 has been obtained by misrepresentation or suppression of any material fact, or (b) the holder of a licence has, without reasonable cause, failed to comply with the conditions subject to which the licence has been granted or has con travened any of the provisions of this Act or the rules made hereunder, then, without prejudice to any other penalty to which the holder of the licence may be liable under this Act, the licensing officer may, after giving the holder of the licence an oppor tunity to be heard, by order in writing, revoke the licence or forfeit the security furnished by him under the proviso to sub -section (2) of section 8 or any part thereof and communicate the order to the holder of the licence: Provided that where the licen sing officer considers it necessary so to do for any special reasons, he may, pending such revocation or forfeiture, by order, suspend the operation of the licence for such period as may be specified in the order and serve, by registered post, such order a long with a statement of the reasons on the holder of the licence and such order shall take effect on the date on which such service is effected.
sub_structure.2: (2) Subject to any rules that may be made in this behalf, the licensing officer may vary or amend a licence granted under section 8.

plain_english_summary: Allows a licensing officer to revoke, suspend, or forfeit the security of a licence obtained by misrepresentation or where the licensee has failed to comply with conditions, and allows amendment of licences.

title: Appeal

sub_structure.1: (1) Any person aggrieved by an order made under section 4, section 5, section 8 or section 10 may, within thirty days from the date on which the order is communicated to him, prefer an appeal to an appellate officer who shall be a person nominated in this behal f by the appropriate Government: Provided that the appellate officer may entertain the appeal after the expiry of the said period of thirty days, if he is satisfied that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from filing the appeal in time.
sub_structure.2: (2) On receipt of an appeal under sub-section (1), the appellate officer shall, after giving the appellant an opportunity of being heard, dispose of the appeal as expeditiously as possible. CHAPTER IV DUTIES AND OBLIGATIONS OF CONTRACTORS

plain_english_summary: Provides a right of appeal, within 30 days, against orders on registration or licensing to an appellate officer, who must dispose of the appeal after giving the appellant a hearing.

title: Duties of contractors

sub_structure.1: (1) It shall be the duty of every contractor— (a) to furnish such particulars and in such form as may be prescribed, to the specified authority in the State from which an inter -State migrant workman is recruited and in the State in which such workman is employed, within fifteen days from the date of recruitment, or, as the case may be, the date of employment, and where any change occurs in any of the particulars so furnished, such change shall be notified to the specified authorities of both the States; (b) to issue to every inter -State migrant workma n, a pass book affixed with a passport size photograph of the workman and indicating in Hindi and English languages, and where the language of the workman is not Hindi or English, also in the language of the workman,— (i) the name and place of the establishment wherein the workman is employed; (ii) the period of employment; (iii) the proposed rates and modes of payment of wages; (iv) the displacement allowance payable; (v) the return fare payable to the workman on the expiry of the period of his employment and in such contingencies as may be prescribed and in such other contingencies as may be specified in the contract of employment; (vi) deductions made; and (vii) such other particulars as may be prescribed; (c) to furnish in respect of every inter -State migrant workman who ceases to be employed, a return in such form and in such manner as may be prescribed, to the specified authority in the State from which he is recruited and in the State in which he is employed, which shall include a declaration that all the wages and other dues payable to the workman and the fare for the return journey back to his State have been paid.
sub_structure.2: (2) The contractor shall maintain the pass book referred to in sub-section (1) up-to-date and cause it to be retained with the inter-State migrant workman concerned. Explanation.—For the purposes of this section and section 16 “specified authority ” means such authority as may be specified by the appropriate Government in this behalf. CHAPTER V WAGES, WELFARE AND OTHER FACILITIES TO BE PROVIDED TO INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN

plain_english_summary: Requires contractors to furnish worker particulars to authorities in both the recruiting and employing States, issue and maintain a pass book recording each migrant workman's employment details, and disclose the terms of employment to the workman.

chapter_title: WAGES, WELFARE AND OTHER FACILITIES TO BE PROVIDED TO INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Wage rates and other conditions of service of inter-State migrant workmen

sub_structure.1: (1) The wage rates, holidays, hours of work and other conditions of service of an inter-State migrant workman shall,— (a) in a case where such workman performs in any establishment, the same or similar kind of work as is being performed by any ot her workman in that establishment, be the same as those applicable to such other workman; and (b) in any other case, be such as may be prescribed by the appropriate Government: Provided that an inter-State migrant workman shall in no case be paid less than the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 (11 of 1948).
sub_structure.2: (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, wages payable to an inter-State migrant workman under this section shall be paid in cash.

plain_english_summary: Requires an inter-State migrant workman to receive wage rates and conditions of service equal to comparable local workmen (or the state-notified minimum wage if no comparable workman exists), and mandates that wages be paid in cash.

chapter_title: WAGES, WELFARE AND OTHER FACILITIES TO BE PROVIDED TO INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Displacement allowance

sub_structure.1: (1) There shall be paid by the contractor to every inter -State migrant workman at the time of recruitment, a displacement al lowance equal to fifty per cent. of the monthly wages payable to him or seventy-five rupees, whichever is higher.
sub_structure.2: (2) The amount paid to a workman as displacement allowance under sub -section ( 1) shall not be refundable and shall be in addition to the wages or other amounts payable to him.

plain_english_summary: Requires contractors to pay a displacement allowance (50% of monthly wages or Rs. 75, whichever is higher) to migrant workmen at recruitment, which is non-refundable and additional to wages.

chapter_title: WAGES, WELFARE AND OTHER FACILITIES TO BE PROVIDED TO INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Journey allowance, etc
text: A journey allowance of a sum not less than the fare from the place of residence of the inter -State migrant workman in his State to t he place of work in the other St ate shall be payable by the contractor to the workman both for the outward and return journeys and such workman shall be entitled to payment of wages during the period of such journeys as if he were on duty.
plain_english_summary: Requires contractors to pay migrant workmen a journey allowance covering travel costs for both outward and return journeys, plus wages for the travel period as if the workman were on duty.

chapter_title: WAGES, WELFARE AND OTHER FACILITIES TO BE PROVIDED TO INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Other facilities
text: It shall be the duty of every contractor employing inter-State migrant workmen in connection with the work of an establishment to which this Act applies,— (a) to ensure regular payment of wages to such workmen; (b) to ensure equal pay for equal work irrespective of sex; (c) to ensure suitable conditions of work to such workmen having regard to the fact that they are required to work in a State different from their own State; (d) to provide and maintain suitable residential accommodation to such workmen during the period of their employment; (e) to provide the prescribed medical facilities to the workmen, free of charge; (f) to provide such protective clothing to the workmen as may be prescribed; and (g) in case of fatal accident or serious bodily injury to any such workman, t o report to the specified authorities of both the States and also the next of kin of the workman.
plain_english_summary: Lists contractor duties toward migrant workmen including timely wage payment, equal pay regardless of sex, suitable working conditions, and providing residential accommodation, medical facilities, protective clothing, and other prescribed welfare facilities.

chapter_title: WAGES, WELFARE AND OTHER FACILITIES TO BE PROVIDED TO INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Responsibility for payment of wages

sub_structure.1: (1) A contractor shall be responsible for payment of wages to each inter -State migrant workman employed by him and su ch wages shall be paid before the expiry of such period as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.2: (2) Every principal employer shall nominate a representative duly authorised by him to be present at the time of disbursement of wages by the contractor and it shall be the duty of such representative to certify the amounts paid as wages in such manner as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.3: (3) It shall be the duty of the contractor to ensure the disbursement of wages in the presence of the authorised representative of the principal employer.
sub_structure.4: (4) In case the contractor fails to make payment of wages within the prescribed period or makes short payment, then the principal employer shall be liable to make payment of the wages in full or the unpaid balance due, as the case may be, to the inter -State migrant workman employed by the contractor and recover the amount so paid from the contractor either by deduction from any amount payable to the contractor under any contract or as a debt payable by the contractor.

plain_english_summary: Makes the contractor primarily responsible for timely wage payment to migrant workmen (in the presence of an authorised representative of the principal employer), with the principal employer becoming liable to pay if the contractor fails to pay in full or on time.

chapter_title: WAGES, WELFARE AND OTHER FACILITIES TO BE PROVIDED TO INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Liability of principal employer in certain cases

sub_structure.1: (1) If any allowance required to be paid under section 14 or section 15 to an inter -State migrant workman employed in an establishment to which this Act applies is not paid by the contractor or if any facility specified in section 16 is not provided for the benefit of such workman, such allowance shall be paid, or, as the case may be, the facility shall be provided, by the principal employer within such time as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.2: (2) All the allowances paid by the principal employer or all the expenses incurred by him in providing the facility referred to in sub-section (1) may be recovered by him from the contractor either by deduction from any amount payable to the contractor under any contract or as a debt payable by the contractor.

plain_english_summary: Makes the principal employer liable to directly provide statutory allowances or facilities to a migrant workman if the contractor fails to do so, while entitling the principal employer to recover those costs from the contractor.

chapter_title: WAGES, WELFARE AND OTHER FACILITIES TO BE PROVIDED TO INTER-STATE MIGRANT WORKMEN
title: Past liabilities
text: It shall be the duty of every contractor and every principal employer to ensure that any loan given by such contractor or principal employer to any inter-State migrant workman does not remain outstanding after the completion of the period of employment of such workman under the said contractor or, as the case may be, in the establishment of such principal employer and accordingly every obligation of an inter-State migrant workman to re-pay any debt obtained by him during the period of his employment from the contractor or the principal employer and remaining unsatisfied before the completion of such period shall, on such completion, be deemed to have been extinguished and no suit or other proceeding shall lie in any court or before any authori ty for the recovery of such debt or any part thereof. CHAPTER VI INSPECTING STAFF
plain_english_summary: Obliges contractors and principal employers to ensure that loans given to migrant workmen are cleared before the end of the workman's employment period, and prevents loan-based bondage.

title: Inspectors

sub_structure.1: (1) The appropriate Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint such persons as it thinks fit to be inspectors for the purposes of this Act, and define the local limits within which they shall exercise their powers under this Act.
sub_structure.2: (2) Subject to any rules made in this behalf, within the local limits for which he i s appointed, an inspector may— (a) if he has reason to believe that any inter-State migrant workmen are employed in any premises or place, enter, at all reasonable hours, with such assistants (if any), being persons in the service of the Government or any local or other public authority as he thinks fit, such premise s or place for the purpose of— (i) satisfying himself whether the provisions of this Act in relation to the payment of wages, conditions of service, or facilities to be provided to such workmen are being complied with; (ii) examining any register or record or notic es required to be kept or exhibited by the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder, and requiring the production thereof for inspection; (b) examine any person found in any such premises or place for the purpose of determining whether such person is an inter-State migrant workman; (c) require any person giving out work to any workman, to give any information, which is in his power to give, with respect to the names and addresses of the persons to, for and from whom the work is given out or received, and with respect to the payments to be made for the work; (d) seize or take copies of such register, record of wages, or notices or portions thereof as he may consider relevant in respect of an offence under this Act which he has reason to believe has been committed by a principal employer or contractor, and (e) exercise such other powers as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.3: (3) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-sections (1) and (2), if a State Government considers it necessary for the purpose of satisfy ing itself that the provisions of this Act are being complied with in respect of any workmen belonging to that State and employed in an establishment situated in another State, it may, by order in writing, appoint such persons, being persons in the service of that Government, for the exercise of such of the powers mentioned in sub-section (2), as may be specified in that order: Provided that no such order shall be issued without the concurrence of the Government of the State in which such workmen are employ ed or where the establishment is an establishment referred to in sub-clause ( i) of clause ( a) of sub -section ( 1) of section 2, without the concurr ence of the Central Government.
sub_structure.4: (4) Any person required to produce any document or thing, or to give any information required, by an inspector under sub -section (2), or by a person appointed under sub -section (3), shall be deemed to be legally bound to do so within the meaning of section 175 and section 176 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).
sub_structure.5: (5) The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974), shall, so far as may be, apply to any search or seizure under this section as they apply to any search or seizure made under the authority of a warrant issued under section 94 of the said Code. CHAPTER VII MISCELLANEOUS

plain_english_summary: Allows the appropriate Government to appoint inspectors with powers to enter premises, examine records and workers, and seize documents, and lets a State Government appoint an inspecting person for establishments under Central Government jurisdiction; also protects against self-incrimination.

title: Inter-State migrant workmen to be deemed to be in employment from date of recruitment for the purposes of certain enactments
text: For the purposes of the enactments specified in the Schedule, an inter-State migrant workman shall, on and from the date of his recruitment, be deemed to be employed and actually worked in the establishment or, as the case may be, the first establishment in connection with the work of which he is employed.
plain_english_summary: Deems a migrant workman to be 'in employment' from the date of recruitment (not just from when work actually begins) for purposes of specified other labour enactments listed in the Schedule.

title: Provisions regarding industrial disputes in relation to inter-State migrant workmen

sub_structure.1: (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in the Industrial Disputes Act. 1947 (14 of 1947), any dispute or difference in connection with the employment or non-employment or the terms of employment or the conditions of labour, of an inter -State migrant workman (hereafter in this section referred to as the industrial dispute), may,— (a) if the industrial dispute is relatable to an establishment referred to in sub-clause ( i) of clause ( a) of sub -section ( 1) of section 2, be referred under the provisions of the said Act, by the Central Government to any of the authorities referred to in Chapter II of that Act (hereafter in this section referred to as the said authorities),— (i) in the State wherein the establishment is situated; (ii) in the State wherein the recruitment of such workman was made if he makes an application in that behalf to that Government on the ground that he has returned to that State after the completion of his employment; (b) if the industrial dispute is relatable to an establishment referred to in sub -clause ( ii) of clause (a) of sub-section (1) of section 2,— (i) be referred under the provisions of the said Act, by the Governme nt of the State wherein the establishment is situated, to any of the said authorities in that State; or (ii) be referred under the pro visions of the said Act, by the Government of the State wherein the recruitment of such workman was made to any of the said authorities in that State, if he makes an application in that behalf to that Government on the ground that he has returned to that State after the completion of his employment: Provided that— (a) no application referred to in sub -clause (ii) of clause ( a) or sub-clause (ii) of clause ( b) shall be entertained after the expiry of a period of six months from the date of his return to the State wherein the recruitment was made after the completion of his employment, unless the Government concerned is satisfie d that the applicant was prevented by sufficient cause from making the application within that period; (b) no reference under the said sub -clause (ii) of clause ( b) shall be made except after obtaining the concurrence of the Government of the State wherein the establishment concerned is situated.
sub_structure.2: (2) Without prejudice to the provisions of section 33B of the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (14 of 1947), where during the pendency of any proceeding in respect of an industrial dispute under that Act before any of the said authorities in the State wherein the establishment is situated, an application is made to that authority by an inter -State migrant workman for the transfer of such proceeding to a corresponding authority in the State wherein his recruitment was made on the ground that he has returned to that State after the completion of his employment, that authority shall forward the application to the Central Government, or, as the case may be, to the Government of the State wherein such recruitment was made and transfer such proceeding in the prescribed manner to such authority as may be specified in this behalf by that Government: Provided that in a case where no authority has been specified by the Government concerned within the prescribed period, the authority before which the proceeding is pending shall, on a request being made by the inter -State migrant workman and after obtaining the previous approval of the Government which referred the dispute to that authority, forward such proceeding to the Government concerned for reference of such dispute to an authority in the State wherein such recruitment was made.
sub_structure.3: (3) Without prejudice to the provisions of sub -section (2), if the Central Government is satisfied that it is expedient in the int erests of justice so to do, it may, by order in writing and for reasons to be stated therein, withdraw any proceeding in respect of any industrial dispute relating to an inter -State migrant workman pending before an authority in the Sta te in which the esta blishment concerned is situated and transfer the same to such authority in the State wherein the recruitment of such workman was made as may be specified in the order.
sub_structure.4: (4) The authority to which any proceeding is transferred under this section may proceed either de novo or from the stage at which it was so transferred.

plain_english_summary: Provides special industrial-disputes procedures for migrant workmen, including power for the Central Government to transfer pending disputes concerning migrant workmen to appropriate authorities in the interest of justice.

title: Registers and other records to be maintained

sub_structure.1: (1) Every principal employer and every contractor shall maintain such registers and records giving such particulars of the inter-State migrant workmen employed, the nature of work performed by such workmen, the rates of wages paid to the workmen and such other particulars in such form as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.2: (2) Every principal employer and every contractor shall keep exhibited in such manner as may be prescribed within the premises of the establishment where the inter-State migrant workmen are employed, notices in the prescribed form containing particulars about the hours of work, nature of duty and such other information as may be prescribed.

plain_english_summary: Requires principal employers and contractors to maintain prescribed registers/records on migrant workmen and to display notices about wage rates and conditions of service at the workplace.

title: Obstructions

sub_structure.1: (1) Whoever obstructs an inspector or a person appointed under sub -section (3) of section 20 (hereinafter referred to as unauthorised person) in the discharge of his duties u nder this Act or refuses or wil fully neglects to afford the inspector or authorised person any reasonable facility for making any inspection, examination, inquiry or investigation authorised by or under this Act in relation to an establishment to which, or a contractor to whom, this Act applies, shall b e punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.
sub_structure.2: (2) Whoever wil fully refuses to produce on the demand of any inspector or authorised person any register or other document kept in pursuance of this Act or prevents or attempts to prevent or does anything which he has reason to believe is likely to prevent any person from app earing before or being examined by any inspector or authorised person acting in pursuance of his duties under this Act, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.

plain_english_summary: Penalizes obstructing an inspector or authorised person, or refusing to produce required registers/documents, with imprisonment up to 3 months and/or a fine up to Rs. 500.

title: Contravention of provisions regarding employment of inter-State migrant workmen
text: Whoever contravenes any provisions of this Act or of any rules made thereunder regulating the employment of inter-State migrant workmen, or contravenes any condition of a licence granted under this Act, shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both, and in the case of a continuing contravention, with an additional fine which may extend to one hundred rupees for every day during which such contravention continues after conviction for the first such contravention.
plain_english_summary: Penalizes contravention of the Act's employment-regulation provisions or licence conditions with imprisonment up to 1 year and/or a fine up to Rs. 1,000, with enhanced penalties for repeat offences.

title: Other offences
text: If any person contravenes any of the provisions of this Act or of any rules made thereunder for which no other penalty is elsewhere provided, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees, or with both.
plain_english_summary: Provides a residual penalty (imprisonment up to 2 years and/or fine up to Rs. 2,000) for any contravention of the Act or rules not otherwise specifically penalized.

title: Offences by companies

sub_structure.1: (1) Where an offence under this Act has been committed by a company, every person who, at the time the offence was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to, the company for the conduct of the business of the company, as well as the company, shall be deemed to be gu ilty of the offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly: Provided that nothing contained in this sub -section shall render any such person liable to any punishment, if he proves that the offence was committed without his kn owledge or that he had exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offence.
sub_structure.2: (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where any offence under this Act has been committed by a company and it is proved that the offence has been committed with the consent or connivance of, or is attributable to any neglect on the part of, any director, manager, secretary or other officer of the company, such director, manager, secretary or other officer shall be deemed to be guilty of that offence and shall be liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly. Explanation.—For the purposes of this section,— (a) “company” means any body corporate and includes a firm or other association of individuals; and (b) “director”, in relation to a firm, means a partner in the firm.

plain_english_summary: Makes company officers in charge of the business personally liable for company offences, subject to a due-diligence defence, with enhanced liability where the offence involved their consent, connivance, or negligence.

title: Cognizance of offences
text: No court shall take cognizance of any offence under this Act except on a complaint made by, or with the previous sanction in writing of, an inspector or authorised person and no court inferior to that of a Metropolitan Magistrate or a Judicial Magistrate of the first class shall try any offence punishable under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Requires that prosecutions be initiated only on complaint by (or with sanction of) an inspector/authorised person, and restricts trial to courts of Metropolitan/first-class Judicial Magistrate or above.

title: Limitation of prosecutions
text: No court shall take cognizance of an offence punishable under this Act unless th e complaint thereof is made within three months from the date on which the alleged commission of the offence came to the knowledge of the inspector or authorised person concerned: Provided that where the offence consists of disobeying a written order made by an inspector or authorised person, complaint thereof may be made within six months of the date on which the offence is alleged to have been committed.
plain_english_summary: Sets a 3-month limitation period (from the inspector's knowledge of the offence) for prosecutions, with a longer period for continuing-order violations.

title: Effect of laws and agreements inconsistent with the Act

sub_structure.1: (1) The provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent therewith contained in any other law or in the terms of any agreement or contract of service, or in any standing orders applicable to the establishment whether made before or after the commencement of this Act: Provided that where under any such law, agreement, contract of service or standing orders, the inter-State migrant workmen employed in the establishment are entitled to benefits in respect of any matter which are more favourable to them than t hose to which they would be entitled under this Act, the inter-State migrant workmen shall continue to be entitled to the more favourable benefits in respect of that matter, notwithstanding that they receive benefits in respect of other matters under this Act.
sub_structure.2: (2) Nothing contained in this Act shall be construed as precluding any inter -State migrant workmen from entering into an agreement with the principal employer or the contractor, as the case may be, for granting them rights or privileges in respect of any matter which are more favourable to them than those to which they would be entitled under this Act.

plain_english_summary: Gives this Act overriding effect over inconsistent laws, agreements, contracts, or standing orders, while still allowing migrant workmen to negotiate additional rights with employers/contractors.

title: Power to exempt in special cases
text: The appropriate Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette and subject to such conditions and restrictions, if any, and for such period or periods as may be specified in the notification, direct that all or any of the provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder shall not apply to or in relation to any establishment or class of establishment s or any contractor or class of contractors or any inter -State migrant workmen in such establishment or class of such workmen, if that Government is satisfied that it is just and proper so to do having regard to the methods of recruitment and the condition s of employment in such establishment or class of establishments and all other relevant circumstances.
plain_english_summary: Allows the appropriate Government to exempt establishments or classes of establishments from all or some provisions of the Act, by notification, subject to conditions.

title: Protection of action taken under the Act

sub_structure.1: (1) No suit, prosecution or other legal proceedings shall lie against any registering officer, licensing officer or any other employee of the Government for anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder.
sub_structure.2: (2) No suit or other legal proceedings shall lie against the Government for any damage caused or likely to be caused by anything which is in good faith done or intended to be done in pursuance of this Act or any rule or notification or order made or issued thereunder.

plain_english_summary: Protects registering/licensing officers and other government employees from suits or prosecution for good-faith action under the Act, and protects the Government itself from liability for good-faith action.

title: Power to give directions
text: The Central Government may give directions to the Government of any State as to the carrying into execution in the State of the provisions contained in this Act.
plain_english_summary: Allows the Central Government to issue directions to State Governments on implementing the Act's provisions.

title: Power to remove difficulties

sub_structure.1: (1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Central Government may , by order published in the Official Gazette, make such provisions not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act, as appears to it to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty: Provided that no such order shall be made after the expiry of tw o years from the date on which this Act comes into force.
sub_structure.2: (2) Every order made under this section shall, as soon as may be after it is made, be laid before each House of Parliament.
