Note: the Appellate Board (IPAB) referred to here was abolished by the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, and its functions were transferred to the High Court — this section's IPAB-era text is preserved for historical/reference purposes.

title: Contravention of secrecy provisions relating to certain inventions
text: If any person fails to comply with a section 35 secrecy direction, or files a foreign patent application in contravention of section 39, they are punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
plain_english_summary: Criminal penalty (up to 2 years' imprisonment and/or fine) for breaching defence-secrecy directions or the foreign-filing-licence requirement — relevant to dual-use or defence-adjacent software/deep-tech inventions.

title: Falsification of entries in register, etc.
text: Making or causing a false register entry, a writing falsely purporting to be a copy of a register entry, or knowingly producing/tendering such false writing in evidence, is punishable with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
plain_english_summary: Criminalises fraudulent tampering with the patent register or fabricating register-extract evidence.

title: Unauthorised claim of patent rights
text: Falsely representing that an article sold is patented in India, or is the subject of a pending Indian patent application, is punishable with a fine up to one lakh rupees.

sub_structure.explanation_1: Explanation 1: marking an article 'patent'/'patented' (or similar) represents it as patented in India; marking 'patent applied for'/'patent pending' (or similar) represents a pending Indian application.
sub_structure.explanation_2: Explanation 2: such markings are deemed to refer to an Indian patent/application unless accompanied by an indication that the patent was obtained/applied for in another country.

plain_english_summary: Criminalises 'patent bluffing' — falsely marking a product as patented (or patent-pending) in India — directly relevant to software/hardware product labelling and marketing claims; penalty is a fine up to Rs 1 lakh.

title: Wrongful use of words "patent office"
text: Using the words "patent office" (or similar words implying official connection to the patent office) on a place of business or issued document, is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both.
plain_english_summary: Prevents private entities from misleadingly branding themselves as officially connected to the Patent Office.
keywords: wrongful use of patent office name

title: Refusal or failure to supply information
text: (1) Refusing/failing to furnish information required under section 100(5) (to Central Government) or section 146 (to the Controller, re: working of patents) is punishable with a fine up to ten lakh rupees.

sub_structure.2: (2) Knowingly or believingly furnishing false information/statements when required is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both.

plain_english_summary: Backs up the Controller's power to demand 'working of patents' statements (section 146) with a substantial fine (up to Rs 10 lakh) for non-compliance, and imprisonment for knowingly false statements — relevant to a startup-patentee's annual compliance filings.

title: Practice by non-registered patent agents
text: Contravening section 129 (practising as an unregistered patent agent) is punishable with a fine up to one lakh rupees for a first offence, and up to five lakh rupees for a second or subsequent offence.
plain_english_summary: Criminal penalty for unauthorised practice as a patent agent, with escalating fines for repeat offences.

title: Offences by companies
text: (1) Where a company commits an offence under this Act, both the company and every person in charge of/responsible for its business at the time are deemed guilty and liable, unless they prove the offence was without their knowledge and they exercised due diligence.

sub_structure.2: (2) Where the offence was committed with a director/manager/secretary/officer's consent, connivance, or attributable neglect, that individual is also deemed guilty.
sub_structure.explanation: Explanation: 'company' includes any body corporate, firm, or association of individuals; 'director' of a firm means a partner.

plain_english_summary: Standard corporate-criminal-liability provision attributing Patent Act offences to a company's responsible officers, subject to a due-diligence defence — relevant to how a startup's founders/officers could be personally exposed for Chapter XX offences committed by the company.

title: Register of patent agents
text: (1) The Controller maintains a register of patent agents recording names, addresses, and other prescribed particulars of qualified persons under section 126.

sub_structure.2: (2) The register may be kept in electronic form subject to prescribed safeguards.

plain_english_summary: Establishes the official register of patent agents — India's equivalent of a registered patent attorney roll.

title: Qualifications for registration as patent agents
text: (1) To register as a patent agent, a person must: (a) be an Indian citizen; (b) be at least 21; (c) hold a science/engineering/technology degree (or equivalent), plus either pass the qualifying examination, or have 10+ years' experience as an examiner or Controller; and (d) pay the prescribed fee.

sub_structure.2: (2) Persons registered before the Patents (Amendment) Act, 2005 may continue to be (or be re-registered as) patent agents on payment of prescribed fees.

plain_english_summary: Sets India's qualification bar for registered patent agents — a science/engineering/technology degree plus a qualifying exam (or long-standing Patent Office experience) — relevant to who a startup may formally engage to prosecute Indian patent applications.

title: Rights of patent agents
text: Every registered patent agent is entitled to practice before the Controller, and to prepare documents, transact business and discharge such other functions as prescribed, in connection with proceedings before the Controller.
plain_english_summary: Confirms the professional rights/scope of practice of a registered patent agent before the Indian Patent Office.

title: Subscription and verification of certain documents by patent agents
text: (1) Applications and communications to the Controller may be signed by a duly authorised patent agent; if the principal is absent from India, they may be signed/verified on their behalf by an authorised patent agent.
plain_english_summary: Allows a patent agent to sign/verify filings on behalf of an applicant, including one located outside India — relevant to foreign-headquartered software companies filing Indian patents through local agents.

title: Restrictions on practice as patent agents
text: (1) No person (alone or in partnership) may practise, describe, or hold themselves out as a patent agent unless registered (and, in partnership, all partners registered). (2) No company/body corporate may practise or hold itself out as a patent agent.

sub_structure.explanation: Explanation: 'practising as a patent agent' includes applying for/obtaining patents, preparing specifications/documents, and giving non-scientific/technical advice on patent validity/infringement.

plain_english_summary: Restricts patent-agent practice to individually registered natural persons (not companies), and defines the scope of regulated 'practice' broadly to include specification drafting and validity/infringement advice.

title: Removal from register of patent agents and restoration
text: (1) The Controller may remove a name from the register, after a hearing and inquiry, where the entry was made by error/misrepresentation/suppression, or the agent was convicted of an offence or found guilty of professional misconduct rendering them unfit.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Controller may, on application and sufficient cause, restore a removed name to the register.

plain_english_summary: The disciplinary mechanism for removing (and potentially restoring) a patent agent's registration for misconduct or conviction.

title: Power of Controller to refuse to deal with certain agents
text: (1) The Controller may refuse to recognise as agent: an individual removed and not restored; a person convicted under section 123; a non-registered person substantially acting as an agent for their employer's benefit; or a company/firm with such a disqualified person as director/manager/partner.

sub_structure.2: (2) The Controller must refuse to recognise as agent any person who neither resides nor has a place of business in India.

plain_english_summary: Gives the Controller gatekeeping power over who may act as agent before the Patent Office, including a mandatory bar on persons/entities without an Indian residence or place of business.

title: Savings in respect of other persons authorised to act as agents
text: Nothing in this Chapter prohibits: (a) an applicant from drafting their own specification or appearing/acting before the Controller; or (b) an advocate (not a patent agent) from taking part in a hearing before the Controller on behalf of a party.
plain_english_summary: Preserves a self-represented applicant's right to act pro se, and an advocate's right to appear at Controller hearings, without needing separate patent-agent registration.

title: Convention countries
text: Any country (or group/union of countries, or intergovernmental organisation) that is a party to an international/regional/bilateral treaty to which India is also a party, and which affords Indian applicants/citizens privileges similar to those given its own citizens for patent grant/protection, is a 'convention country' under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Defines the reciprocity basis for 'convention country' status, which underlies convention-priority filings under sections 135-139 (India's equivalent of Paris Convention priority claims).

title: Notification as to countries not providing for reciprocity
text: Where a notified country does not accord Indian citizens the same patent rights it accords its own nationals, that country's nationals cannot apply for, or be registered as proprietor/assignee of, an Indian patent, or hold/apply for a licence under one.
plain_english_summary: A reciprocity-enforcement tool — the Central Government can bar nationals of non-reciprocating countries from applying for, holding, or licensing Indian patents.

title: Convention applications
text: (1) Where a person files a 'basic application' in a convention country and files the corresponding Indian application within twelve months, the priority date of claims based on the basic application's disclosure is the basic application's filing date.

sub_structure.explanation: Explanation: where similar protection was sought in multiple convention countries, the twelve months runs from the earliest such application.
sub_structure.2: (2) A single convention application may cover cognate/related inventions from multiple convention-country applications, filed within twelve months of the earliest.

plain_english_summary: The core convention-priority mechanism — files an Indian application within 12 months of a first foreign filing (e.g. a US provisional) and claims that earlier priority date, the standard Paris Convention route most software startups use for their first Indian filing after filing abroad.

title: Special provisions relating to convention application
text: (1) Every convention application must be accompanied by a complete specification, specify the date/country of the first foreign application, and state no earlier convention-country application was made for the invention.

sub_structure.3: (3) A convention application cannot be post-dated under section 17(1) beyond the date on which it could otherwise have been made.

plain_english_summary: Sets the specific formal content and dating requirements for convention (Paris Convention priority) applications filed in India.

title: Multiple priorities
text: (1) Where related inventions were the subject of multiple convention-country applications constituting one invention, a single application may be filed within twelve months of the earliest, covering the inventions in the basic applications' specifications.

sub_structure.2: (2) The priority date of a claim based on matter in one or more basic applications is the date that matter was first disclosed.

plain_english_summary: Allows combining multiple related foreign priority filings into one Indian application, with each claim taking the priority date of whichever basic application first disclosed its subject matter.

title: Supplementary provisions as to convention applications
text: (1)-(2) On request, the applicant must furnish verified copies (and English translations, if foreign-language) of the corresponding foreign specification/documents.

sub_structure.4: (4) A PCT international application designating India has effect as a filing under sections 7, 54 and 135, with its title/description/claims/abstract/drawings treated as the complete specification.
sub_structure.5: (5) The filing date for such applications is the international filing date under the PCT.

plain_english_summary: Supplements the convention-application regime, and critically confirms that PCT national-phase entries into India are treated exactly like domestic applications with the international filing date preserved — the operative rule for PCT-based Indian patent strategy.

title: Other provisions of Act to apply to convention applications
text: Save as otherwise provided in this Chapter, all other provisions of the Act apply to a convention application and any patent granted on it, as they apply to an ordinary application/patent.
plain_english_summary: A general saving clause confirming convention applications are otherwise treated identically to ordinary Indian applications throughout prosecution, grant, and enforcement.

title: Avoidance of certain restrictive conditions
text: (1) It is unlawful to insert, in a contract for sale/lease of a patented article (or article made by a patented process), or in a licence to manufacture/use a patented article or to work a patented process, a condition that: (a) ties the purchaser/lessee/licensee to acquiring non-patented articles only from the vendor/lessor/licensor or their nominees (or restricts acquiring them elsewhere); (b) prohibits or restricts using a non-patented article not supplied by the vendor/lessor/licensor; (c) prohibits or restricts using a non-patented process other than the patented one; or (d) imposes exclusive grant-back, prevents challenges to the patent's validity, or amounts to coercive package licensing. Any such condition is void.

sub_structure.2: (2) Splitting such a condition into a separately-executed agreement does not exempt it from this section.
sub_structure.3: (3) In an infringement proceeding, it is a defence to prove an unlawful condition of this kind was in force under a contract relating to the patent — unless the plaintiff is not a party to that contract and proves the condition was inserted without their knowledge/consent.
sub_structure.4: (4) This section does not: (a) affect a condition prohibiting sale of goods other than a particular person's; (b) validate an otherwise-invalid contract; or (c) affect a lease/licence condition reserving to the lessor/licensor the right to supply replacement parts or repair the patented article.

plain_english_summary: India's anti-tying and anti-abusive-licensing-term provision for patents — directly parallel to section 42 of the Designs Act. Void per se are: exclusive-sourcing/tying clauses, restrictions on using competing non-patented products/processes, exclusive grant-back obligations, no-challenge (non-assertion of invalidity) clauses, and coercive package/bundled licensing. This is the single most important provision to check when drafting or reviewing a patent licence agreement for a software-related invention — common SaaS/technology licensing clauses like 'you may not challenge the validity of our patents' or 'you must license our entire patent bundle, not individual patents' risk being struck down as void under this section, with a defendant able to raise the illegal condition as a full defence to an infringement claim.

title: Determination of certain contracts
text: (1) Once all patents protecting a product/process covered by a sale/lease/manufacture/use/licence contract have ceased to be in force, the purchaser/lessee/licensee may terminate that contract (notwithstanding any contrary term) by giving three months' written notice.

sub_structure.2: (2) This is without prejudice to any other right to terminate the contract that exists independently of this section.

plain_english_summary: Gives a patent licensee/purchaser a statutory right to exit a patent-related contract once the underlying patent(s) expire — a mandatory 'sunset' termination right that overrides contrary contract terms (e.g. a fixed multi-year term that would otherwise survive patent expiry), relevant when structuring the term/termination clauses of a patent licence agreement.

title: Fees
text: (1) Prescribed fees are payable for the grant of patents, applications, and other prescribed matters relating to patent grant. (2) The Controller need not act until a payable fee is paid. (3) A document requiring a fee is deemed not filed if the fee isn't paid within the prescribed time.

sub_structure.4: (4) Where a principal patent is granted more than two years after filing, fees that fell due in the meantime may be paid within three months of the patent being recorded (extendable to nine months).

plain_english_summary: The general fee-payment framework underlying all Patent Office transactions, including a grace period for fees that accrue during a long pendency before grant.

title: Restrictions upon publication of specification
text: Subject to Chapter VII (secrecy), an application and any specification filed with it shall not, without the applicant's consent, be published before expiry of the section 11A(1) prescribed period, or before it becomes open for public inspection under section 11A(3) or section 43.
plain_english_summary: Confirms the confidentiality of applications/specifications before the statutory publication trigger points, subject to the applicant's own consent to earlier publication.

title: Reports of examiners to be confidential
text: Examiners' reports to the Controller are not open to public inspection or publication, and are not liable to production/inspection in legal proceedings unless the court certifies production/inspection is desirable in the interests of justice.
plain_english_summary: Keeps internal examiner reports confidential by default, shielding the Patent Office's internal deliberative process from routine discovery — a court order is needed to unseal them.

title: Publication of official journal
text: The Controller shall periodically publish an official journal containing information required to be published under the Act or rules.
plain_english_summary: The statutory basis for the Patent Office's official journal, through which applications, grants, oppositions and other statutory notices are published.

title: Power of Controller to call for information from patentees
text: (1) The Controller may, by written notice, require a patentee or licensee (exclusive or otherwise) to furnish, within two months (or longer, if allowed), information/statements on the extent to which the patented invention has been commercially worked in India.

sub_structure.2: (2) Every patentee and licensee must, independently, furnish prescribed 'working' statements at prescribed intervals (not less than six months).
sub_structure.3: (3) The Controller may publish information received under this section.

plain_english_summary: Requires every Indian patentee (and licensee) to periodically file statements on how far the patented invention is being commercially worked in India — the statutory 'Form 27' working-statement obligation, backed by penalties under section 122, and a key ongoing compliance duty for any startup that holds a granted Indian patent.

title: Evidence of entries, documents, etc.
text: (1) A Controller-signed certificate as to any authorised entry/matter/thing is prima facie evidence of it. (2) A certified copy of a register entry, document, or patent is admissible in evidence in all courts without further proof of the original.

sub_structure.3: (3) The Controller/patent office officers are not compellable, in proceedings to which they are not a party, to produce the register/documents or testify, absent special court order.

plain_english_summary: Simplifies proof of Patent Office records in litigation — certified copies are self-authenticating evidence, and Patent Office staff are generally shielded from being compelled to testify.

title: Declaration by infant, lunatic etc.
text: (1) Where a person is incapable (due to minority, lunacy, or other disability) of making a statement/doing an act required under this Act, their lawful guardian/committee/manager (or a court-appointed person) may act on their behalf.

sub_structure.2: (2) The court may appoint such a person on petition by anyone acting on the disabled person's behalf, or any other interested person.

plain_english_summary: Allows a guardian or court-appointed representative to act for an inventor/applicant who is a minor or under a legal disability.

title: Service of notices, etc., by post
text: Any notice, application or document required/authorised under this Act may be given, made or filed by post.
plain_english_summary: Confirms postal service is an acceptable method for Patent Act notices and filings.

title: Security for costs
text: Where a party giving notice of opposition, or applying for a compulsory licence, neither resides nor carries on business in India, the Controller may require security for costs, and may treat the opposition/application as abandoned if security is not given.
plain_english_summary: Protects Indian respondents from costs-recovery difficulties against foreign opponents/applicants by allowing the Controller to demand upfront security for costs.

title: Transmission of orders of courts to Controller
text: (1) Every High Court/Appellate Board order on a revocation petition (including validity certificates) must be sent to the Controller for entry in the register.

sub_structure.2: (2) Where a court's infringement/section 106 suit decides claim validity, the court must transmit its judgment/decree to the Controller for entry in a supplemental record.

plain_english_summary: Ensures court and Appellate Board decisions on patent validity/revocation are formally recorded in the official register, keeping it synchronized with litigation outcomes.

title: Information relating to patents
text: A person requesting prescribed information about a specified patent or patent application, in the prescribed manner and on payment of the prescribed fee, is entitled to have that information supplied.
plain_english_summary: Provides a formal statutory information-request channel to obtain prescribed details about a specific patent/application from the Patent Office.

title: Loss or destruction of patents
text: If a patent document is lost or destroyed (or its non-production is satisfactorily explained), the Controller may, on application and payment of the prescribed fee, issue a sealed duplicate.
plain_english_summary: Allows a patentee to obtain a replacement sealed patent document if the original is lost or destroyed.

title: Reports of Controller to be placed before Parliament
text: The Central Government shall cause an annual report on the execution of this Act by/under the Controller to be placed before both Houses of Parliament.
plain_english_summary: Requires annual parliamentary reporting on the Patent Office's administration of the Act — a transparency/accountability mechanism.

title: Patent to bind Government
text: Subject to the Act's other provisions, a patent has the like effect against the Government as it has against any person.
plain_english_summary: Confirms patents are generally enforceable against the Government itself, subject to the Chapter XVII carve-outs for authorised Government use/acquisition.

title: Right of Government to sell or use forfeited articles
text: Nothing in this Act affects the Government's (or its successors-in-title's) power to sell or use articles forfeited under any other law in force.
plain_english_summary: A narrow saving clause preserving the Government's power over separately-forfeited articles regardless of patent status.

title: Protection of security of India
text: Notwithstanding anything in this Act, the Central Government shall (a) not disclose information about a patentable invention/application it considers prejudicial to India's security, and (b) may take any action (including patent revocation) it considers necessary for India's security, by Gazette notification.

sub_structure.explanation: Explanation: 'security of India' includes matters relating to fissionable materials, arms/ammunition/war-materiel traffic, or actions taken in wartime or other international-relations emergencies.

plain_english_summary: A broad national-security override letting the Central Government withhold sensitive patent information or revoke a patent outright wherever it considers this necessary for India's security — a sweeping and largely unreviewable power added by the 2002 amendment, with obvious relevance to dual-use/defence-adjacent technology.

title: Power of High Courts to make rules
text: The High Court may make rules, consistent with this Act, as to the conduct and procedure of proceedings before it under this Act.
plain_english_summary: Delegated rule-making power letting each High Court set its own procedural rules for patent litigation before it.

title: Power of Central Government to make rules
text: (1) The Central Government may, by Gazette notification, make rules to carry out the Act's purposes.

sub_structure.2_selected: (2) Without prejudice to that generality, rules may cover matters such as: application/specification filing formats and timelines; fees and payment timing; examiner-report matters; procedure for disposing of pre-grant representations (s.25(1)) and s.39 applications; notice forms/timing; register maintenance (including electronic form); scientific-adviser qualifications (s.115); Appellate Board staff salaries/procedure and appeal forms/fees (ss.117, 117A, 117D); patent-agent register maintenance and qualifying examinations (s.125); and indexing/abridgement of specifications.
sub_structure.3: (3) Rule-making is subject to prior publication of draft rules, unless the Central Government dispenses with this where circumstances make it impracticable.

plain_english_summary: The Central Government's general delegated rule-making power (implemented via the Patents Rules, 2003) covering the detailed procedural machinery of the Act — fees, forms, timelines, and electronic recordkeeping — subject to a public-comment (prior-publication) requirement.

title: Rules to be placed before Parliament
text: Every rule made under this Act shall be laid before each House of Parliament for a total of thirty days (in one or more sessions); both Houses may modify or annul it within that window, without prejudice to anything already done under the rule.
plain_english_summary: The standard 30-day parliamentary 'laying' requirement for delegated rules under the Act, mirroring the equivalent provisions in the Designs and Trade Marks Acts.

title: Repeal of Act 2 of 1911 in so far as it relates to patents and savings
text: (1) The Indian Patents and Designs Act, 1911, so far as it relates to patents, is repealed, with the said 1911 Act amended as specified in the Schedule (relating to designs, which the 1911 Act continued to govern until the Designs Act, 2000).

sub_structure.4: (4) This section's specific mentions do not prejudice the General Clauses Act, 1897's general application to repeals.
sub_structure.5: (5) Pending infringement suits/revocation proceedings at the Act's commencement may continue and be disposed of as if this Act had not been passed.

plain_english_summary: The repeal-and-savings clause transitioning from the 1911 Act to this Act, preserving pending litigation and leaving the 1911 Act's design provisions (as amended by the Schedule) temporarily in force until superseded by the Designs Act, 2000.

CHAPTER II ADMINISTRATION

title: Officers under this Act
text:
The Government shall, by notification, appoint
the following classes of officers for the purposes of this Act, namely:––

sub_structure.a:
Principal Chief Commissioners of Central Tax or Principal Directors General
of Central Tax,
sub_structure.b: Chief Commissioners of Central Tax or Directors General of Central Tax,
sub_structure.c:
Principal Commissioners of Central Tax or Principal Additional Directors
General of Central Tax,
sub_structure.d:
Commissioners of Central Tax or Additional Directors General of Central
Tax,
sub_structure.e:
Additional Commissioners of Central Tax or Additional Directors of
Central Tax,
sub_structure.f: Joint Commissioners of Central Tax or Joint Directors of Central Tax,
sub_structure.g: Deputy Commissioners of Central Tax or Deputy Directors of Central Tax,
sub_structure.h:
Assistant Commissioners of Central Tax or Assistant Directors of
Central Tax, and
sub_structure.i:
any other class of officers as it may deem fit:
Provided that the officers appointed under the Central Excise Act, 1944 shall be
deemed to be the officers appointed under the provisions of this Act.

title: Appointment of Officers

sub_structure.1:
The Board may, in addition to the officers
as may be notified by the Government under section 3, appoint such persons as it may
think fit to be the officers under this Act.
sub_structure.2:
Without prejudice to the provisions of sub-section (1), the Board may, by
order, authorise any officer referred to in clauses (a) to (h) of section 3 to appoint officers of
central tax below the rank of Assistant Commissioner of central tax for the administration
of this Act.
20
CHAPTER II ADMINISTRATION

title: Powers of officers under GST

sub_structure.1:
Subject to such conditions and
limitations as the Board may impose, an officer of central tax may exercise the powers and
discharge the duties conferred or imposed on him under this Act.
sub_structure.2:
An officer of central tax may exercise the powers and discharge the duties
conferred or imposed under this Act on any other officer of central tax who is subordinate
to him.
sub_structure.3:
The Commissioner may, subject to such conditions and limitations as may
be specified in this behalf by him, delegate his powers to any other officer who is
subordinate to him.
sub_structure.4:
Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, an Appellate
Authority shall not exercise the powers and discharge the duties conferred or imposed on
any other officer of central tax.

title: Authorisation of officers of State tax or Union territory tax as proper officer in certain circumstances

sub_structure.1:
Without prejudice to the provisions of this Act,
the officers appointed under the State Goods and Services Tax Act or the Union Territory
Goods and Services Tax Act are authorised to be the proper officers for the purposes of
this Act, subject to such conditions as the Government shall, on the recommendations of
the Council, by notification, specify.
sub_structure.2:
Subject to the conditions specified in the notification issued under
sub-section (1),––
sub_structure.a:
where any proper officer issues an order under this Act, he shall also issue an
order under the State Goods and Services Tax Act or the Union Territory Goods and
Services Tax Act, as authorised by the State Goods and Services Tax Act or the Union
Territory Goods and Services Tax Act, as the case may be, under intimation to the
jurisdictional officer of State tax or Union territory tax;

title: Tax liability on composite and mixed supplies
text:
The tax liability on a
composite or a mixed supply shall be determined in the following manner, namely:—

sub_structure.a:
a composite supply comprising two or more supplies, one of which is a
principal supply, shall be treated as a supply of such principal supply; and
sub_structure.b:
a mixed supply comprising two or more supplies shall be treated as a supply
of that particular supply which attracts the highest rate of tax.

title: Levy and collection

sub_structure.1:
Subject to the provisions of sub-section (2), there
shall be levied a tax called the central goods and services tax on all intra-State supplies of
goods or services or both, except on the supply of alcoholic liquor for human
consumption, on the value determined under section 15 and at such rates, not exceeding
twenty per cent., as may be notified by the Government on the recommendations of the
Council and collected in such manner as may be prescribed and shall be paid by the
taxable person.
sub_structure.2:
The central tax on the supply of petroleum crude, high speed diesel, motor
spirit (commonly known as petrol), natural gas and aviation turbine fuel shall be levied
with effect from such date as may be notified by the Government on the
recommendations of the Council.
sub_structure.3:
The Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by
notification, specify categories of supply of goods or services or both, the tax on which
shall be paid on reverse charge basis by the recipient of such goods or services or both and
all the provisions of this Act shall apply to such recipient as if he is the person liable for
paying the tax in relation to the supply of such goods or services or both.

title: Time of Supply of Goods

sub_structure.1:
The liability to pay tax on goods shall arise
at the time of supply, as determined in accordance with the provisions of this section.
sub_structure.2:
The time of supply of goods shall be the earlier of the following dates,
namely:—
sub_structure.a:
the date of issue of invoice by the supplier or the last date on which he is
required, under [******]32 section 31, to issue the invoice with respect to the supply; or
sub_structure.b:
the date on which the supplier receives the payment with respect to the
supply:
Provided that where the supplier of taxable goods receives an amount up to one
thousand rupees in excess of the amount indicated in the tax invoice, the time of supply
to the extent of such excess amount shall, at the option of the said supplier, be the date of
issue of invoice in respect of such excess amount.
Explanation 1.––For the purposes of clauses (a) and (b), ―supply‖ shall be deemed
to have been made to the extent it is covered by the invoice or, as the case may be, the
payment.
Explanation 2.––For the purposes of clause (b), ―the date on which the supplier
receives the payment‖ shall be the date on which the payment is entered in his books of
account or the date on which the payment is credited to his bank account, whichever is
earlier.
sub_structure.3:
In case of supplies in respect of which tax is paid or liable to be paid on
reverse charge basis, the time of supply shall be the earliest of the following dates,
namely:—
sub_structure.a_2: the date of the receipt of goods; or
sub_structure.b_2:
the date of payment as entered in the books of account of the recipient or the

date on which the payment is debited in his bank account, whichever is earlier; or

Provided that where it is not possible to determine the time of supply under clause
sub_structure.a_3:
or clause (b) or clause (c), the time of supply shall be the date of entry in the books of

sub_structure.4: In case of supply of vouchers by a supplier, the time of supply shall be—

title: Change in rate of tax in respect of supply of goods or services
text:
Notwithstanding anything contained in section 12 or section 13, the time of supply, where
there is a change in the rate of tax in respect of goods or services or both, shall be
determined in the following manner, namely:––

sub_structure.a:
in case the goods or services or both have been supplied before the change
in rate of tax,––
sub_structure.i:
where the invoice for the same has been issued and the payment is also
received after the change in rate of tax, the time of supply shall be the date of receipt of
payment or the date of issue of invoice, whichever is earlier; or
sub_structure.ii:
where the invoice has been issued prior to the change in rate of tax but
payment is received after the change in rate of tax, the time of supply shall be the date of
issue of invoice; or
sub_structure.b:
in case the goods or services or both have been supplied after the change in
34
CHAPTER IV TIME AND VALUE OF SUPPLY
rate of tax,––
sub_structure.i_2:
where the payment is received after the change in rate of tax but the
invoice has been issued prior to the change in rate of tax, the time of supply shall be the date
of receipt of payment; or
sub_structure.ii_2:
where the invoice has been issued and payment is received before the
change in rate of tax, the time of supply shall be the date of receipt of payment or date of
issue of invoice, whichever is earlier; or
sub_structure.iii_2:
where the invoice has been issued after the change in rate of tax but the
payment is received before the change in rate of tax, the time of supply shall be the date of
issue of invoice:
Provided that the date of receipt of payment shall be the date of credit in the bank
account if such credit in the bank account is after four working days from the date of
change in the rate of tax.
Explanation.––For the purposes of this section, ―the date of receipt of payment‖
shall be the date on which the payment is entered in the books of account of the supplier
or the date on which the payment is credited to his bank account, whichever is earlier.

title: Value of Taxable Supply

sub_structure.1:
The value of a supply of goods or services
or both shall be the transaction value, which is the price actually paid or payable for the
said supply of goods or services or both where the supplier and the recipient of the supply
are not related and the price is the sole consideration for the supply.
sub_structure.2: The value of supply shall include–––
sub_structure.a:
any taxes, duties, cesses, fees and charges levied under any law for the time
being in force other than this Act, the State Goods and Services Tax Act, the Union
Territory Goods and Services Tax Act and the Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to
States) Act, if charged separately by the supplier;
sub_structure.c:
incidental expenses, including commission and packing, charged by the
35
CHAPTER IV TIME AND VALUE OF SUPPLY
supplier to the recipient of a supply and any amount charged for anything done by the
supplier in respect of the supply of goods or services or both at the time of, or before
delivery of goods or supply of services;
sub_structure.d:
interest or late fee or penalty for delayed payment of any consideration for
any supply; and
sub_structure.e:
subsidies directly linked to the price excluding subsidies provided by the
Central Government and State Governments.
Explanation.––For the purposes of this sub-section, the amount of subsidy shall be
included in the value of supply of the supplier who receives the subsidy.
sub_structure.3: The value of the supply shall not include any discount which is given––
sub_structure.a_2:
before or at the time of the supply if such discount has been duly recorded in
the invoice issued in respect of such supply; and
sub_structure.b_2: after the supply has been effected, if—
sub_structure.i:
such discount is established in terms of an agreement entered into at or
before the time of such supply and specifically linked to relevant invoices; and
sub_structure.ii:
input tax credit as is attributable to the discount on the basis of document
issued by the supplier has been reversed by the recipient of the supply.
sub_structure.4:
Where the value of the supply of goods or services or both cannot be
determined under sub-section (1), the same shall be determined in such manner as may be
prescribed.
sub_structure.5:
Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) or sub-section (4),
the value of such supplies as may be notified by the Government on the recommendations
of the Council shall be determined in such manner as may be prescribed.
Explanation.—For the purposes of this Act,––
sub_structure.a_3: persons shall be deemed to be ―related persons‖ if––
sub_structure.i_2: such persons are officers or directors of one another‘s businesses;
sub_structure.iii: such persons are employer and employee;
sub_structure.iv:
any person directly or indirectly owns, controls or holds twenty-five per
cent. or more of the outstanding voting stock or shares of both of them;
sub_structure.v: one of them directly or indirectly controls the other;
sub_structure.vi: both of them are directly or indirectly controlled by a third person;
sub_structure.vii: together they directly or indirectly control a third person; or
sub_structure.viii: they are members of the same family;
sub_structure.b_3: the term ―person‖ also includes legal persons;

title: Eligibility and conditions for taking input tax credit

sub_structure.1:
Every
registered person shall, subject to such conditions and restrictions as may be prescribed
and in the manner specified in section 49, be entitled to take credit of input tax charged on
any supply of goods or services or both to him which are used or intended to be used in the
course or furtherance of his business and the said amount shall be credited to the
electronic credit ledger of such person.
sub_structure.2:
Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, no registered person
shall be entitled to the credit of any input tax in respect of any supply of goods or services
or both to him unless,––

under this Act, or such other tax paying documents as may be prescribed;

title: Apportionment of credit and blocked credits

sub_structure.1:
Where the goods or
services or both are used by the registered person partly for the purpose of any business
and partly for other purposes, the amount of credit shall be restricted to so much of the
input tax as is attributable to the purposes of his business.
sub_structure.2:
Where the goods or services or both are used by the registered person
partly for effecting taxable supplies including zero-rated supplies under this Act or under the
Integrated Goods and Services Tax Act and partly for effecting exempt supplies under the
said Acts, the amount of credit shall be restricted to so much of the input tax as is
attributable to the said taxable supplies including zero-rated supplies.
sub_structure.3:
The value of exempt supply under sub-section (2) shall be such as may be
prescribed, and shall include supplies on which the recipient is liable to pay tax on reverse
charge basis, transactions in securities, sale of land and, subject to clause (b) of paragraph

shall lapse:
Provided that the option once exercised shall not be withdrawn during the

title: Availability of credit in special circumstances

sub_structure.1:
Subject to such
conditions and restrictions as may be prescribed—
sub_structure.a:
a person who has applied for registration under this Act within thirty days
from the date on which he becomes liable to registration and has been granted such
registration shall be entitled to take credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock and
inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock on the day immediately
preceding the date from which he becomes liable to pay tax under the provisions of this
Act;
sub_structure.b:
a person who takes registration under sub-section (3) of section 25 shall be
entitled to take credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock and inputs contained in
semi-finished or finished goods held in stock on the day immediately preceding the date of
grant of registration;
sub_structure.c:
where any registered person ceases to pay tax under section 10, he shall be
entitled to take credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock, inputs contained in semi-
finished or finished goods held in stock and on capital goods on the day immediately preceding
the date from which he becomes liable to pay tax under section 9:
Provided that the credit on capital goods shall be reduced by such percentage
points as may be prescribed;
sub_structure.d:
where an exempt supply of goods or services or both by a registered person
becomes a taxable supply, such person shall be entitled to take credit of input tax in
respect of inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held
in stock relatable to such exempt supply and on capital goods exclusively used for such
exempt supply on the day immediately preceding the date from which such supply
becomes taxable:
Provided that the credit on capital goods shall be reduced by such percentage
points as may be prescribed.

sub_structure.2:
A registered person shall not be entitled to take input tax credit under
sub-section (1) in respect of any supply of goods or services or both to him after the expiry
of one year from the date of issue of tax invoice relating to such supply.
sub_structure.3:
Where there is a change in the constitution of a registered person on
account of sale, merger, demerger, amalgamation, lease or transfer of the business with
the specific provisions for transfer of liabilities, the said registered person shall be allowed to
transfer the input tax credit which remains unutilised in his electronic credit ledger to such
sold, merged, demerged, amalgamated, leased or transferred business in such manner as
may be prescribed.
sub_structure.4:
Where any registered person who has availed of input tax credit opts to
pay tax under section 10 or, where the goods or services or both supplied by him become
wholly exempt, he shall pay an amount, by way of debit in the electronic credit ledger or
electronic cash ledger, equivalent to the credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock
and inputs contained in semi-finished or finished goods held in stock and on capital goods,
reduced by such percentage points as may be prescribed, on the day immediately
preceding the date of exercising of such option or, as the case may be, the date of such
exemption:
Provided that after payment of such amount, the balance of input tax credit, if
any, lying in his electronic credit ledger shall lapse.
sub_structure.5:
The amount of credit under sub-section (1) and the amount payable under
sub-section (4) shall be calculated in such manner as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.6:
In case of supply of capital goods or plant and machinery, on which input tax
credit has been taken, the registered person shall pay an amount equal to the input tax
credit taken on the said capital goods or plant and machinery reduced by such percentage
points as may be prescribed or the tax on the transaction value of such capital goods or
plant and machinery determined under section 15, whichever is higher:
Provided that where refractory bricks, moulds and dies, jigs and fixtures are
supplied as scrap, the taxable person may pay tax on the transaction value of such goods
determined under section 15.

title: Taking input tax credit in respect of inputs and capital goods sent for job work

sub_structure.1:
The principal shall, subject to such conditions and restrictions as may be
prescribed, be allowed input tax credit on inputs sent to a job worker for job work.
sub_structure.2:
Notwithstanding anything contained in clause (b) of sub-section (2) of
section 16, the principal shall be entitled to take credit of input tax on inputs even if the
inputs are directly sent to a job worker for job work without being first brought to his place
of business.
sub_structure.3:
Where the inputs sent for job work are not received back by the principal
after completion of job work or otherwise or are not supplied from the place of business of
the job worker in accordance with clause (a) or clause (b) of sub-section (1) of section 143
within one year of being sent out, it shall be deemed that such inputs had been supplied
by the principal to the job worker on the day when the said inputs were sent out:
Provided that where the inputs are sent directly to a job worker, the period of one
year shall be counted from the date of receipt of inputs by the job worker.
sub_structure.4:
The principal shall, subject to such conditions and restrictions as may be
prescribed, be allowed input tax credit on capital goods sent to a job worker for job work.
sub_structure.5:
Notwithstanding anything contained in clause (b) of sub-section (2) of
section 16, the principal shall be entitled to take credit of input tax on capital goods even
if the capital goods are directly sent to a job worker for job work without being first
brought to his place of business.
sub_structure.6:
Where the capital goods sent for job work are not received back by the
principal within a period of three years of being sent out, it shall be deemed that such
capital goods had been supplied by the principal to the job worker on the day when the
said capital goods were sent out:
Provided that where the capital goods are sent directly to a job worker, the period
of three years shall be counted from the date of receipt of capital goods by the job worker.
sub_structure.7:
Nothing contained in sub-section (3) or sub-section (6) shall apply to
moulds and dies, jigs and fixtures, or tools sent out to a job worker for job work.
Explanation.––For the purpose of this section, ―principal‖ means the person

title: Manner of distribution of credit by Input Service Distributor

sub_structure.1:
The
Input Service Distributor shall distribute the credit of central tax as central tax or integrated
tax and integrated tax as integrated tax or central tax, by way of issue of a document
containing the amount of input tax credit being distributed in such manner as may be
prescribed.
sub_structure.2:
The Input Service Distributor may distribute the credit subject to the
following conditions, namely:––
sub_structure.a:
the credit can be distributed to the recipients of credit against a document
containing such details as may be prescribed;
sub_structure.b:
the amount of the credit distributed shall not exceed the amount of credit
available for distribution;
sub_structure.c:
the credit of tax paid on input services attributable to a recipient of credit shall
be distributed only to that recipient;
sub_structure.d:
the credit of tax paid on input services attributable to more than one recipient
of credit shall be distributed amongst such recipients to whom the input service is
attributable and such distribution shall be pro rata on the basis of the turnover in a State or
turnover in a Union territory of such recipient, during the relevant period, to the
aggregate of the turnover of all such recipients to whom such input service is attributable
and which are operational in the current year, during the said relevant period;
sub_structure.e:
the credit of tax paid on input services attributable to all recipients of credit
shall be distributed amongst such recipients and such distribution shall be pro rata on the
basis of the turnover in a State or turnover in a Union territory of such recipient, during
the relevant period, to the aggregate of the turnover of all recipients and which are
operational in the current year, during the said relevant period.
Explanation.––For the purposes of this section,––
sub_structure.a_2: the ―relevant period‖ shall be––
sub_structure.i:
if the recipients of credit have turnover in their States or Union territories
in the financial year preceding the year during which credit is to be distributed, the said

sub_structure.ii:
if some or all recipients of the credit do not have any turnover in their States
or Union territories in the financial year preceding the year during which the credit is to
be distributed, the last quarter for which details of such turnover of all the recipients are
available, previous to the month during which credit is to be distributed;
sub_structure.c_2:
the term ‗‗turnover‘‘, in relation to any registered person engaged in the

turnover, reduced by the amount of any duty or tax levied under [entries 84 and 92A]40 of

title: Manner of recovery of credit distributed in excess
text:
Where the Input
Service Distributor distributes the credit in contravention of the provisions contained
in section 20 resulting in excess distribution of credit to one or more recipients of
credit, the excess credit so distributed shall be recovered from such recipients along
with interest, and the provisions of section 73 or section 74, as the case may be, shall,
mutatis mutandis, apply for determination of amount to be recovered.

from where he makes a taxable supply of goods or services or both, if his aggregate
turnover in a financial year exceeds twenty lakh rupees:
Provided that where such person makes taxable supplies of goods or services or
both from any of the special category States, he shall be liable to be registered if his

title: Procedure for registration

sub_structure.1:
Every person who is liable to be registered
under section 22 or section 24 shall apply for registration in every such State or Union
territory in which he is so liable within thirty days from the date on which he becomes
liable to registration, in such manner and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed:
Provided that a casual taxable person or a non-resident taxable person shall apply
for registration at least five days prior to the commencement of business:

under the said Act in order to be eligible for grant of registration.
[(6A) Every registered person shall undergo authentication, or furnish proof of
possession of Aadhaar number, in such form and manner and within such time as may
be prescribed:
Provided that if an Aadhaar number is not assigned to the registered person, such
person shall be offered alternate and viable means of identification in such manner as
Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, prescribe:
Provided further that in case of failure to undergo authentication or furnish proof
of possession of Aadhaar number or furnish alternate and viable means of identification,
registration allotted to such person shall be deemed to be invalid and the other provisions
of this Act shall apply as if such person does not have a registration.
sub_structure.6B:
On and from the date of notification, every individual shall, in order to be
eligible for grant of registration, undergo authentication, or furnish proof of possession of
Aadhaar number, in such manner as the Government may, on the recommendations of
the Council, specify in the said notification:
Provided that if an Aadhaar number is not assigned to an individual, such
individual shall be offered alternate and viable means of identification in such manner as
the Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, specify in the said
notification.
sub_structure.6C:
On and from the date of notification, every person, other than an individual,
shall, in order to be eligible for grant of registration, undergo authentication, or furnish
proof of possession of Aadhaar number of the Karta, Managing Director, whole time
Director, such number of partners, Members of Managing Committee of Association,
Board of Trustees, authorised representative, authorised signatory and such other class of
persons, in such manner, as the Government may, on the recommendations of the
Council, specify in the said notification:
53
CHAPTER VI REGISTRATION
Provided that where such person or class of persons have not been assigned the
Aadhaar Number, such person or class of persons shall be offered alternate and viable
means of identification in such manner as the Government may, on the
recommendations of the Council, specify in the said notification.
sub_structure.6D:
The provisions of sub-section (6A) or sub-section (6B) or sub-section (6C)
shall not apply to such person or class of persons or any State or Union territory or part
thereof, as the Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, specify by
notification.
Explanation.—For the purposes of this section, the expression ―Aadhaar number‖
shall have the same meaning as assigned to it in clause (a) of section 2 of the Aadhaar
(Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act, 2016.]48
sub_structure.7:
Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (6), a non-resident
taxable person may be granted registration under sub-section (1) on the basis of such other
documents as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.8:
Where a person who is liable to be registered under this Act fails to obtain
registration, the proper officer may, without prejudice to any action which may be taken
under this Act or under any other law for the time being in force, proceed to register such
person in such manner as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.9: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1),––
sub_structure.a:
any specialised agency of the United Nations Organisation or any
Multilateral Financial Institution and Organisation notified under the United Nations
(Privileges and Immunities) Act, 1947, Consulate or Embassy of foreign countries; and
sub_structure.b:
any other person or class of persons, as may be notified by the Commissioner,
shall be granted a Unique Identity Number in such manner and for such purposes,
including refund of taxes on the notified supplies of goods or services or both received by
them, as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.10:
The registration or the Unique Identity Number shall be granted or rejected
48 Inserted by The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2019 (No. 23 of 2019) – Brought into force w.e.f. 01st January,
2020.
54
CHAPTER VI REGISTRATION
after due verification in such manner and within such period as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.11:
A certificate of registration shall be issued in such form and with effect from
such date as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.12:
A registration or a Unique Identity Number shall be deemed to have been
granted after the expiry of the period prescribed under sub-section (10), if no deficiency
has been communicated to the applicant within that period.

title: Deemed registration

sub_structure.1:
The grant of registration or the Unique Identity
Number under the State Goods and Services Tax Act or the Union Territory Goods and
Services Tax Act shall be deemed to be a grant of registration or the Unique Identity
Number under this Act subject to the condition that the application for registration or the
Unique Identity Number has not been rejected under this Act within the time specified in
sub-section (10) of section 25.
sub_structure.2:
Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (10) of section 25, any
rejection of application for registration or the Unique Identity Number under the State
Goods and Services Tax Act or the Union Territory Goods and Services Tax Act shall be
deemed to be a rejection of application for registration under this Act.

title: Special provisions relating to casual taxable person and non-resident taxable person

sub_structure.1:
The certificate of registration issued to a casual taxable person or a
non- resident taxable person shall be valid for the period specified in the application for
registration or ninety days from the effective date of registration, whichever is earlier and
such person shall make taxable supplies only after the issuance of the certificate of
registration:
Provided that the proper officer may, on sufficient cause being shown by the said
taxable person, extend the said period of ninety days by a further period not exceeding
ninety days.
sub_structure.2:
A casual taxable person or a non-resident taxable person shall, at the time
of submission of application for registration under sub-section (1) of section 25, make an
advance deposit of tax in an amount equivalent to the estimated tax liability of such
person for the period for which the registration is sought:
55
CHAPTER VI REGISTRATION
Provided that where any extension of time is sought under sub-section (1), such
taxable person shall deposit an additional amount of tax equivalent to the estimated tax
liability of such person for the period for which the extension is sought.
sub_structure.3:
The amount deposited under sub-section (2) shall be credited to the
electronic cash ledger of such person and shall be utilised in the manner provided
under section 49.

title: Amendment of registration

sub_structure.1:
Every registered person and a person to
whom a Unique Identity Number has been assigned shall inform the proper officer of any
changes in the information furnished at the time of registration or subsequent thereto, in
such form and manner and within such period as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.2:
The proper officer may, on the basis of information furnished under sub-
section (1) or as ascertained by him, approve or reject amendments in the registration
particulars in such manner and within such period as may be prescribed:
Provided that approval of the proper officer shall not be required in respect of
amendment of such particulars as may be prescribed:
Provided further that the proper officer shall not reject the application for
amendment in the registration particulars without giving the person an opportunity of
being heard.
sub_structure.3:
Any rejection or approval of amendments under the State Goods and
Services Tax Act or the Union Territory Goods and Services Tax Act, as the case may be,
shall be deemed to be a rejection or approval under this Act.

title: Cancellation [or suspension]49 of registration

sub_structure.1:
The proper officer
may, either on his own motion or on an application filed by the registered person or by
his legal heirs, in case of death of such person, cancel the registration, in such manner
and within such period as may be prescribed, having regard to the circumstances where,–
sub_structure.a:
the business has been discontinued, transferred fully for any reason including
death of the proprietor, amalgamated with other legal entity, demerged or otherwise
49 Inserted by The Central Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Act, 2018 (No. 31 of 2018) – Brought
into force w.e.f. 01st February, 2019.
56
CHAPTER VI REGISTRATION
disposed of; or
sub_structure.b: there is any change in the constitution of the business; or
sub_structure.c:
the taxable person, other than the person registered under sub-section (3) of
section 25, is no longer liable to be registered under section 22 or section 24.
[Provided that during pendency of the proceedings relating to cancellation of
registration filed by the registered person, the registration may be suspended for such
period and in such manner as may be prescribed.]50
sub_structure.2:
The proper officer may cancel the registration of a person from such date,
including any retrospective date, as he may deem fit, where,––
sub_structure.a_2:
a registered person has contravened such provisions of the Act or the rules
made thereunder as may be prescribed; or
sub_structure.b_2:
a person paying tax under section 10 has not furnished returns for three
consecutive tax periods; or
sub_structure.c_2:
any registered person, other than a person specified in clause (b), has not
furnished returns for a continuous period of six months; or
sub_structure.d:
any person who has taken voluntary registration under sub-section (3) of
section 25 has not commenced business within six months from the date of
registration; or
sub_structure.e:
registration has been obtained by means of fraud, wilful misstatement or
suppression of facts:
Provided that the proper officer shall not cancel the registration without giving the
person an opportunity of being heard:
[Provided further that during pendency of the proceedings relating to cancellation
of registration, the proper officer may suspend the registration for such period and in such
manner as may be prescribed.]51
50 Inserted by The Central Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Act, 2018 (No. 31 of 2018) – Brought
into force w.e.f. 01st February, 2019.
51 Inserted by The Central Goods and Services Tax (Amendment) Act, 2018 (No. 31 of 2018) – Brought
into force w.e.f. 01st February, 2019.
57
CHAPTER VI REGISTRATION
sub_structure.3:
The cancellation of registration under this section shall not affect the liability
of the person to pay tax and other dues under this Act or to discharge any obligation under
this Act or the rules made thereunder for any period prior to the date of cancellation
whether or not such tax and other dues are determined before or after the date of
cancellation.
sub_structure.4:
The cancellation of registration under the State Goods and Services Tax Act
or the Union Territory Goods and Services Tax Act, as the case may be, shall be deemed
to be a cancellation of registration under this Act.
sub_structure.5:
Every registered person whose registration is cancelled shall pay an
amount, by way of debit in the electronic credit ledger or electronic cash ledger, equivalent
to the credit of input tax in respect of inputs held in stock and inputs contained in semi-
finished or finished goods held in stock or capital goods or plant and machinery on the day
immediately preceding the date of such cancellation or the output tax payable on such
goods, whichever is higher, calculated in such manner as may be prescribed:
Provided that in case of capital goods or plant and machinery, the taxable person
shall pay an amount equal to the input tax credit taken on the said capital goods or plant
and machinery, reduced by such percentage points as may be prescribed or the tax on the
transaction value of such capital goods or plant and machinery under section 15,
whichever is higher.
sub_structure.6:
The amount payable under sub-section (5) shall be calculated in such
manner as may be prescribed.

title: Revocation of cancellation of registration

sub_structure.1:
Subject to such
conditions as may be prescribed, any registered person, whose registration is cancelled by
the proper officer on his own motion, may apply to such officer for revocation of
cancellation of the registration in the prescribed manner within thirty days from the date of
service of the cancellation order.
[Provided that the registered person who was served notice under sub-section (2)
of section 29 in the manner as provided in clause (c) or clause (d) of sub-section (1) of
section 169 and who could not reply to the said notice, thereby resulting in cancellation
of his registration certificate and is hence unable to file application for revocation of
58
CHAPTER VI REGISTRATION
cancellation of registration under sub-section (1) of section 30 of the Act, against such
order passed up to 31.03.2019, shall be allowed to file application for revocation of
cancellation of the registration not later than 22.07.2019]52
sub_structure.2:
The proper officer may, in such manner and within such period as may be
prescribed, by order, either revoke cancellation of the registration or reject the application:
Provided that the application for revocation of cancellation of registration shall not
be rejected unless the applicant has been given an opportunity of being heard.
sub_structure.3:
The revocation of cancellation of registration under the State Goods and
Services Tax Act or the Union Territory Goods and Services Tax Act, as the case may be,
shall be deemed to be a revocation of cancellation of registration under this Act.
52 Inserted vide Order No. 05/2019-GST dated 23.04.2020
59
CHAPTER VII TAX INVOICE, CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTES
CHAPTER VII TAX INVOICE, CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTES

chapter_title: TAX INVOICE, CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTES
title: Tax invoice

sub_structure.1:
A registered person supplying taxable goods shall,
before or at the time of,—
sub_structure.a:
removal of goods for supply to the recipient, where the supply involves
movement of goods; or
sub_structure.b:
delivery of goods or making available thereof to the recipient, in any other
case,
issue a tax invoice showing the description, quantity and value of goods, the tax
charged thereon and such other particulars as may be prescribed:
Provided that the Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by
notification, specify the categories of goods or supplies in respect of which a tax invoice
shall be issued, within such time and in such manner as may be prescribed.
sub_structure.2:
A registered person supplying taxable services shall, before or after the
provision of service but within a prescribed period, issue a tax invoice, showing the
description, value, tax charged thereon and such other particulars as may be prescribed:
Provided that the Government may, on the recommendations of the Council, by
notification and subject to such conditions as may be mentioned therein, specify the
categories of services in respect of which—
sub_structure.a_2:
any other document issued in relation to the supply shall be deemed to
be a tax invoice; or
sub_structure.b_2: tax invoice may not be issued.
sub_structure.3: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-sections (1) and (2)––
sub_structure.a_3:
a registered person may, within one month from the date of issuance of
certificate of registration and in such manner as may be prescribed, issue a revised invoice
against the invoice already issued during the period beginning with the effective date of
registration till the date of issuance of certificate of registration to him;
sub_structure.b_3:
a registered person may not issue a tax invoice if the value of the goods or
services or both supplied is less than two hundred rupees subject to such conditions and
60
CHAPTER VII TAX INVOICE, CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTES
in such manner as may be prescribed;
sub_structure.c:
a registered person supplying exempted goods or services or both or paying
tax under the provisions of section 10 shall issue, instead of a tax invoice, a bill of supply
containing such particulars and in such manner as may be prescribed:
Provided that the registered person may not issue a bill of supply if the value of the
goods or services or both supplied is less than two hundred rupees subject to such
conditions and in such manner as may be prescribed;
sub_structure.e:
where, on receipt of advance payment with respect to any supply of goods or
services or both the registered person issues a receipt voucher, but subsequently no supply
is made and no tax invoice is issued in pursuance thereof, the said registered person may
issue to the person who had made the payment, a refund voucher against such payment;
sub_structure.f:
a registered person who is liable to pay tax under sub-section (3) or sub-
section (4) of section 9 shall issue an invoice in respect of goods or services or both
received by him from the supplier who is not registered on the date of receipt of goods or
services or both;
sub_structure.g:
a registered person who is liable to pay tax under sub-section (3) or sub-
section (4) of section 9 shall issue a payment voucher at the time of making payment to
the supplier.
sub_structure.4:
In case of continuous supply of goods, where successive statements of
accounts or successive payments are involved, the invoice shall be issued before or at the
time each such statement is issued or, as the case may be, each such payment is received.
sub_structure.5:
Subject to the provisions of clause (d) of sub-section (3), in case of
continuous supply of services,––
sub_structure.a_4:
where the due date of payment is ascertainable from the contract, the invoice
shall be issued on or before the due date of payment;
sub_structure.b_4:
where the due date of payment is not ascertainable from the contract, the
61
CHAPTER VII TAX INVOICE, CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTES
invoice shall be issued before or at the time when the supplier of service receives the
payment;
sub_structure.c_2:
where the payment is linked to the completion of an event, the invoice shall
be issued on or before the date of completion of that event.
sub_structure.6:
In a case where the supply of services ceases under a contract before the
completion of the supply, the invoice shall be issued at the time when the supply ceases
and such invoice shall be issued to the extent of the supply made before such cessation.
sub_structure.7:
Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), where the goods
being sent or taken on approval for sale or return are removed before the supply takes
place, the invoice shall be issued before or at the time of supply or six months from the date
of removal, whichever is earlier.
Explanation.––For the purposes of this section, the expression ―tax invoice‖ shall
include any revised invoice issued by the supplier in respect of a supply made earlier.
[31A. Facility of digital payment to recipient.— (1) The Government may, on
the recommendations of the Council, prescribe a class of registered persons who shall
provide prescribed modes of electronic payment to the recipient of supply of goods or
services or both made by him and give option to such recipient to make payment
accordingly, in such manner and subject to such conditions and restrictions, as may be
prescribed.]53

chapter_title: TAX INVOICE, CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTES
title: Prohibition of unauthorised collection of tax

sub_structure.1:
A person who is not a
registered person shall not collect in respect of any supply of goods or services or both
any amount by way of tax under this Act.
sub_structure.2:
No registered person shall collect tax except in accordance with the
provisions of this Act or the rules made thereunder.

chapter_title: TAX INVOICE, CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTES
title: Amount of tax to be indicated in tax invoice and other documents
text:
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or any other law for the time being in
force, where any supply is made for a consideration, every person who is liable to pay tax
53 Inserted by The Finance (No. 2) Act, 2019 (No. 23 of 2019) – Brought into force w.e.f. 01st January,
2020.
62
CHAPTER VII TAX INVOICE, CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTES
for such supply shall prominently indicate in all documents relating to assessment, tax
invoice and other like documents, the amount of tax which shall form part of the price at
which such supply is made.

chapter_title: TAX INVOICE, CREDIT AND DEBIT NOTES
title: Credit and debit notes

sub_structure.1:
[Where one or more tax invoices have]54
been issued for supply of any goods or services or both and the taxable value or tax
charged in that tax invoice is found to exceed the taxable value or tax payable in respect
of such supply, or where the goods supplied are returned by the recipient, or where goods
or services or both supplied are found to be deficient, the registered person, who has
supplied such goods or services or both, may issue to the recipient [one or more credit
notes for supplies made in a financial year]55 containing such particulars as may be
prescribed.
sub_structure.2:
Any registered person who issues a credit note in relation to a supply of
goods or services or both shall declare the details of such credit note in the return for the
month during which such credit note has been issued but not later than September
following the end of the financial year in which such supply was made, or the date of
furnishing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier, and the tax liability shall be
adjusted in such manner as may be prescribed:
Provided that no reduction in output tax liability of the supplier shall be
permitted, if the incidence of tax and interest on such supply has been passed on to any
other person.
sub_structure.3:
[Where one or more tax invoices have]56 been issued for supply of any
goods or services or both and the taxable value or tax charged in that tax invoice is found
to be less than the taxable value or tax payable in respect of such supply, the registered
person, who has supplied such goods or services or both, shall issue to the recipient [one or
more debit notes for supplies made in a financial year]57 containing such particulars as

may be prescribed.
sub_structure.4:
Any registered person who issues a debit note in relation to a supply of
goods or services or both shall declare the details of such debit note in the return for the
month during which such debit note has been issued and the tax liability shall be adjusted
in such manner as may be prescribed.
Explanation.––For the purposes of this Act, the expression ―debit note‖ shall
include a supplementary invoice.
